$comment: ShellX Cut verb registry — the public contract. Single source of truth: the server loads this file, MCP tools are generated from it (dots→underscores), the typed UI client mirrors it, and the coverage gate asserts REST and MCP both expose 100% of these verbs. Envelope: {ok, result?, op_ids?, project_revision?, warnings?[], error?{code,message,clip_id?,at_ms?,cause,suggested_action?}}. Optional mutation_controls are merged into every live verb input schema: op-emitting calls persist request identity, enforce expected_revision atomically, and replay completed lost-response retries. Warnings carry non-fatal guardrail findings in-band rather than only in logs. File-writing verbs such as render.final{path} and export.*{path} fence output paths through canonicalization, traversal and symlink rejection, allowed roots, and suffix allowlists. REST path = POST /api/verb/{name}.

request_id.description: Caller-generated retry identity. For an op-emitting mutation, the same caller + request_id + payload returns the original durable response; a changed payload conflicts.

expected_revision.description: Optional optimistic concurrency guard. Requires request_id and must match the current durable project_revision when the first op commits.

project_revision.description: Latest durable operation ID after a successful project mutation

warnings.description: Non-fatal guardrail findings (e.g. preflight fps/resolution auto-conform). Integrity violations hard-error instead.

verbs.name: project.create
verbs.description: Create a new project directory with default tracks (v1 video, a1t audio), empty op-log, receipts/ and proxies/ subdirs. Becomes the server's open project. dir defaults to a managed <ShellX Cut Projects>/<name>.cutproj under the OS home (~/Documents/ShellX Cut Projects/ on Windows, ~/ShellX Cut Projects/ on macOS/Linux), falling back to <cwd> only when no home resolves. When settings are omitted, the internal 1920x1080@30 fallback is automatically replaced by the first imported video's source width, height, and frame rate while the format remains untouched. starter:first-edit installs the bundled synthetic tutorial clip inside the new project and returns its path for normal media.import.

settings.description: Optional explicit timeline composition settings. The internal fallback is 1920x1080@30, 48kHz; when omitted, the first imported video adopts its source width, height, and frame rate while the format remains untouched.

dir.description: Target .cutproj directory path; default is the managed ShellX Cut Projects directory under the OS home, with <cwd> used only when no home resolves

starter.description: Optional bundled project starter. first-edit installs the self-owned synthetic tutorial clip and returns starter_asset_path; it is not imported until media.import is called.

verbs.result: {path, project, starter_asset_path?} plus envelope op_ids/project_revision — absolute .cutproj path, full project.json state, initial project.create op, and optional bundled starter media path

verbs.name: project.open
verbs.description: Open an existing .cutproj directory. Rebuilds project.json from ops.jsonl if the cache is missing or corrupt. Before activation, scans project-local screen-record checkpoint journals: only a dead owner with a contiguous, independently playable finalized checkpoint prefix may be remuxed to recovered.mp4; live or ambiguous owners are never signalled, and corrupt journals fail closed into quarantine. The returned recovery_scan is an immediate report; screen_record.recovery_status is the durable, paginated receipt projection after navigation.

path.description: Path to the .cutproj directory

verbs.result: {path, project, project_revision, recovery_scan:{recovered:[capture_id], deferred:[detail], failed_closed:[detail]}} — the loaded project state and latest durable op id; recovery_scan reports this activation scan only. Query screen_record.recovery_status for durable per-capture receipt/loss state.

verbs.name: project.list
verbs.description: List recent projects from the global index (~/.shellx-cut/projects.json), reconciled against the managed projects dir + the filesystem: projects whose .cutproj vanished are flagged missing:true, and un-indexed .cutproj dirs found in the managed dir are discovered and added. READ-ONLY discovery — reopen a listed project with project.open{path}. The index is updated as a side-effect of project.create/open/rename.

sort.description: Order: recent (last-opened desc, default) | name (asc) | created (newest first).

q.description: Case-insensitive name or tag substring filter.

verbs.result: {projects: [{id, name, path, created_ms, last_opened_ms, thumb?, duration_ms?, clip_count?, missing?}]}

verbs.name: project.forget
verbs.description: Drop a project from the recent index by id OR path, or bulk-forget every DEAD entry with missing:true. Does NOT delete the .cutproj on disk (forget ≠ delete) — the project can be re-discovered by project.list if it still lives in the managed dir, or reopened by path. missing:true drops every entry whose .cutproj directory does not exist on disk AT CALL TIME (a fresh per-entry check, never the stored missing flag — a project on a remounted drive survives); this is the registry-hygiene path for the ghosts that deleted test/scratch projects leave behind. Pass exactly one of id/path/missing.

path.description: The project's .cutproj path (alternative to id).

missing.description: true ⇒ bulk mode: forget EVERY index entry whose .cutproj no longer exists on disk. Returns {forgotten, removed: N}. Mutually exclusive with id/path.

verbs.result: {forgotten: bool, removed?: int}

verbs.name: project.delete
verbs.description: PERMANENTLY delete a project's .cutproj directory from disk AND drop it from the recent index (forget = index only; delete = the files). DESTRUCTIVE — the UI confirms before calling. GUARDRAILS: the resolved path must be an existing *.cutproj DIRECTORY, and it must NOT be the currently-open project (open/create another first → error conflict). Source MEDIA referenced by the project lives OUTSIDE the .cutproj (linked by path) and is NEVER touched — only the project's own dir (edits/proxies/receipts) is removed. Pass exactly one of id/path.

path.description: The project's .cutproj path (alternative to id).

verbs.result: {deleted: bool, path: string, forgotten: bool}

verbs.name: project.save
verbs.description: Force-write project.json (the cache) to disk. Normally automatic after every applied op; exists for belt-and-braces agent flows.
verbs.result: {saved: true, path}

verbs.name: project.state
verbs.description: Return the materialized project state, or a bounded revision delta when since_revision is current enough. Linked Motion media clips include a transient replay-backed motion_link with current local availability and a bounded path-free keying/roto summary; these machine-local fields are not persisted in project.json.

since_revision.description: Last applied project revision. Returns a bounded applicable delta when every missed op has a safe client patch; otherwise returns a full snapshot with sync.mode:'snapshot' and a reason.

limit.description: Maximum missed operations considered for a delta (default 128).

verbs.result: full project state with project_revision and sync:{mode:'snapshot',reason,...}, or {sync:{mode:'delta',from_revision,project_revision,ops,changes,affected,encoded_bytes}}; no_project if no project is open. Linked media clips may carry motion_link.effects:{schema:'shellx-cut/motion-effects-summary@1',available,ownership:'motion',editableInCut:false,keyedLayerCount?,rotoLayerCount?,trackedRotoLayerCount?,truncated?,layers?}

verbs.name: project.health
verbs.description: Read a bounded, path-free Health & Recovery report for the open project. It first strictly revalidates the journal identity. A live external-change or identity failure is disclosed as journal attention/unavailable and deliberately returns no asset membership until the project is closed and reopened. When the journal is current, each page checks at most 128 registered assets for source, proxy and filmstrip availability. The first page also reports a bounded apparent-byte inventory of only recognized flat rebuildable proxy and thumbnail outputs, including how much is no longer referenced by the project. Its read-only cleanup preview divides those unreferenced outputs by a 24-hour file-change safety window; this is not last-use evidence or permission to delete, and active producers must be rechecked before any future removal. It never follows symlinks or descends into unexpected directories and excludes exports, captures, receipts, source media, and foreign files. The first page returns an opaque project_revision; every cursor continuation must send that exact revision so pages cannot mix project membership across an edit. This read never repairs, deletes, promotes, or follows an unregistered derived path. Job persistence notices are intentionally reported by jobs.list and capture-recovery inventory by screen_record.recovery_status.

cursor.description: Asset id returned as next_cursor by the prior page. Requires revision and means strictly after that stable asset-id cursor.

revision.description: Opaque project_revision from the first page. Required with cursor; a changed revision fails with restart guidance rather than mixing pages.

limit.description: Maximum registered assets examined in this page (default 64).

verbs.result: {schema:'shellx-cut/project-health/1',project_revision?,journal:{status:'verified'|'recovered'|'attention'|'unavailable',log_records?,cache:'matched'|'rebuilt',snapshot:{status:'not_present'|'verified'|'rejected',prefix_ops?},notices:[{code,message,discarded_bytes?,discarded_start?,discarded_end?}]},editing_cache?:{status:'ready'|'partial',bytes,files,reclaimable_bytes,reclaimable_files,cleanup_preview:{status:'ready'|'blocked',minimum_age_ms,aged_unreferenced_bytes,aged_unreferenced_files,recent_unreferenced_bytes,recent_unreferenced_files},latest_modified_ms?,categories:[{kind:'proxies'|'thumbnails',status:'ready'|'partial',bytes,files,reclaimable_bytes,reclaimable_files,scanned_entries,skipped_entries,truncated,entry_limit,latest_modified_ms?}]},media:{status:'ready'|'unavailable',asset_count,checked_count,page:{offline,proxy_available,proxy_missing,proxy_not_recorded,proxy_not_applicable,filmstrip_available,filmstrip_missing,filmstrip_not_recorded,filmstrip_not_applicable},assets:[{asset,source:'available'|'offline',proxy:'available'|'missing'|'not_recorded'|'not_applicable',filmstrip:'available'|'missing'|'not_recorded'|'not_applicable'}],limit,cursor?,next_cursor?,has_more}}. `editing_cache` is first-page-only, path-free, bounded apparent usage for recognized flat rebuildable proxies/thumbnails. `reclaimable_*` counts recognized outputs not referenced by current asset metadata. `cleanup_preview` divides those facts by a 24-hour minimum file-change age and blocks on an incomplete scan; it is informational, does not prove last use or inactive producers, and is not a delete authorization. Symlinks, unexpected directories/files, exports, captures, receipts, and source media are excluded and make the scan partial when encountered. `next_cursor` is present only while `has_more` is true. Page counters describe only returned assets; aggregate every revision-bound page before claiming whole-project healthy. No paths are returned and no delete runs.

verbs.name: project.sequence_list
verbs.description: List the independently editable timelines in the open project. Legacy projects expose one implicit Main sequence until the first sequence mutation. Read-only.
verbs.result: {active_sequence, sequences:[{id, name, active, duration_ms, clip_count, settings}]}

verbs.name: project.sequence_index
verbs.description: Read-only searchable Sequence Index across every timeline in the open project. Returns path-light clip and marker metadata with stable sequence/track/item IDs and timeline ranges, including inactive sequences, so a user or agent can filter and navigate without opening sequences one by one. Text search is case-insensitive and matches all whitespace-separated terms against sequence name, track metadata, clip/asset labels, effect names, live offline state, and marker label/note/color. The status filter can isolate offline media, timeline gaps, effect-bearing clips, and clips on hidden/locked/muted tracks. Anonymous timeline gaps are returned only when status is gaps/issues or the text query explicitly asks for gap/gaps, preserving the default clip/marker index. Source paths are never returned.

query.description: Optional case-insensitive text query. Every whitespace-separated term must match the row metadata. Empty lists the filtered index.

track_kind.description: Optional clip-track filter. When set, marker rows are excluded.

status.description: Optional live clip/status filter. issues includes offline media plus explicit timeline gaps; non-all values exclude marker rows. Gap rows are synthetic path-light clip rows addressed by track and timeline position, not mutable clip IDs.

verbs.result: {query, kind, sequence?, track_kind?, status, total, clip_count, marker_count, issue_count, effect_clip_count, truncated, results:[clip {kind:'clip',sequence_id,sequence_name,active,id,at_ms,end_ms,track_id,track_kind,clip_kind:'media'|'caption'|'gap',label,asset?,src_in_ms?,src_out_ms?,effect_count,effects,offline,track_visible,track_locked,track_muted,issues} | marker {kind:'marker',sequence_id,sequence_name,active,id,at_ms,end_ms,label,note?,color?}]}

verbs.name: project.sequence_create
verbs.description: Create and activate a new sequence in the open project. from:empty creates default video/audio tracks; from:active duplicates the active sequence's complete composition state. Assets and reusable galleries remain shared. Replay-safe and establishes the new sequence's undo baseline.
verbs.result: {sequence:{id, name, active, duration_ms, clip_count, settings}, active_sequence}; one op appended

verbs.name: project.sequence_switch
verbs.description: Save the active sequence's composition state and activate another sequence. Undo, redo, checkpoints, revert, and restore remain scoped to the selected sequence.
verbs.result: {active_sequence}; one op appended

verbs.name: project.sequence_rename
verbs.description: Rename one sequence without changing the project name or timeline state. Sequence names are unique within the project.
verbs.result: {id, name}; one op appended

verbs.name: project.sequence_delete
verbs.description: Delete an inactive sequence from the open project. The active sequence is protected; switch first. Shared project assets are never deleted.
verbs.result: {deleted:true, id}; one op appended

verbs.name: project.ops
verbs.description: Return one bounded cursor page of op-log records from the validated in-memory journal index (incremental sync for review rails).

since.description: A checkpoint id/name OR a raw op id; return only ops strictly after it (a checkpoint resolves to its op, so you get the ops after the checkpoint). Same ref rules as project.diff{from}.

cursor.description: Raw op-id cursor returned as next_cursor by the previous page. Mutually exclusive with since.

verbs.result: {ops: OpRecord[], cursor?, next_cursor?, has_more, limit, encoded_bytes, undo_available, redo_available, project_revision} in log order; next_cursor is present only when has_more is true, while project_revision remains the current reconnect cursor on the final page; no_project if no project is open

verbs.name: project.checkpoint
verbs.description: Record a named checkpoint pointing at the current op-log head. Checkpoints are pointers, never copies. IS an op itself.
verbs.result: {checkpoint: {id, name, at_op, ts}}; one op appended

verbs.name: project.revert
verbs.description: Revert the timeline to a checkpoint or op id by APPENDING one atomic op with the materialized target timeline (the log is never rewritten). Optional if_tip is an atomic optimistic-concurrency guard: a stale history head returns conflict without mutating the project.

to.description: Checkpoint id/name or op id to revert to

if_tip.description: Optional optimistic-concurrency guard: revert only when this op id is still the current history tip

verbs.result: {reverted_to, op_ids} — the appended restore-op ids; stale if_tip returns conflict and appends nothing

verbs.name: project.undo
verbs.description: Step the linear edit-history cursor back ONE edit and set the timeline to that older state — the Ctrl+Z primitive. Unlike edit.restore{tip} (which makes each restore the new tip, so a 2nd undo redid it), this moves a cursor: undoing twice lands on a strictly OLDER state, never the redo. APPENDS one project.undo nav op with its materialized timeline result; the cursor is reconstructed from journal navigation records on reopen, so redo remains available. Refuses with a guardrail at the baseline (nothing to undo). For a deliberate jump to a checkpoint/op use project.revert{to}; for selective non-tip undo use edit.restore{mode:rebase}.
verbs.result: {to_op, cursor, undo_available, redo_available}; one op appended

verbs.name: project.redo
verbs.description: Step the linear edit-history cursor FORWARD one edit (re-applying an edit you undid) and set the timeline to that state — the Ctrl+Shift+Z / Ctrl+Y primitive, the counterpart of project.undo. APPENDS one project.redo nav op with its materialized timeline result. A fresh edit after an undo clears the redo branch (standard behavior). Navigation records reconstruct the cursor on reopen, preserving eligible redo. Refuses with a guardrail at the tip (nothing to redo).
verbs.result: {to_op, cursor, undo_available, redo_available}; one op appended

verbs.name: project.diff
verbs.description: Diff between two log positions (checkpoint id/name, op id, or 'now' = the log head): the ops in between plus a computed summary (clips added/removed/moved, duration delta, per-track ranges touched). Canonical pre-render review: {from: last_checkpoint, to: 'now'}.
verbs.result: DiffSummary {from_op, to_op, ops, clips_added, clips_removed, clips_moved, duration_delta_ms, tracks_touched}

verbs.name: project.close
verbs.description: Close the open project (saves first). Subsequent project-scoped verbs error with code no_project until create/open.
verbs.result: {closed: true}

verbs.name: project.rename
verbs.description: Rename the project's DISPLAY NAME (the human-facing label shown in the title bar). Logged as a non-timeline op so it survives reopen/revert (the name is otherwise set by the project.create op). The .cutproj directory on disk is NOT renamed — the project path is fixed at create; this changes the label only.

name.description: The new project display name (trimmed; must be non-empty)

verbs.result: {name}

verbs.name: project.format
verbs.description: Set the timeline composition FORMAT — canvas resolution (width×height) and frame timing. The first imported video adopts these automatically on a new untouched project. This is not an export-quality picker: delivery aspect, output size, codec, and bitrate can be chosen per render/export without mutating the project. At least one of width/height/fps is required; the rest are left unchanged. Changing fps deterministically regrids existing frame-aware speed ramps to the new output frame/sample grid and reapplies their safe per-frame segment cap. A temporary lower FPS reduces only the effective filtergraph detail; the retained bounded request is restored if a later format permits it. Historic ramps recorded before frame-aware timing retain their millisecond behavior. The format snapshot is logged for replay, so the same regrid order survives reopen. UI: Render > Timeline, with 2160p/1080p/720p/480p and 24/25/30/50/60 fps presets.
verbs.result: {width, height, fps}

verbs.name: project.color
verbs.description: Set the project's COLOR MANAGEMENT — the WORKING color space (the renderer converts each clip into it before grade/effects) and the OUTPUT color space (the delivered file's tagging + final pixels). A lightweight color-management workflow (ffmpeg zscale, not a full ACES engine). Supported spaces: rec709 (the DEFAULT — in and out), rec2020 (UHD/wide-gamut), srgb (sRGB display/screen-capture), linear (scene-linear working space). Every conversion among these four is supported via zscale; an unknown name is rejected with the supported list. At least one of working/output is required; the other is left unchanged. DEFAULT rec709/rec709 = today's behavior — a default config emits NO color transform, so the render is byte-identical to a pre-color-management render (setting it back to rec709/rec709 restores that). Recorded as a non-timeline metadata op like project.format — the config lives in the project file and survives reopen/revert. Forces the SOFTWARE render path (the zscale conversion is CPU + bit-exact).

working.description: Working color space (renderer composites/grades in it). Default rec709.

output.description: Output/delivery color space (final file tagging + pixels). Default rec709.

verbs.result: {working, output}

verbs.name: project.brand
verbs.description: Replace or clear the project's durable brand kit. The complete saved snapshot can pin caption fonts, palette, position, size bounds, and delivery aspect; verify.brand uses it by default and render.bundle automatically enforces it when brand_ref is omitted. Recorded as a non-timeline metadata op, so it survives replay and reopen. Pass exactly one of brand or clear:true.

brand.description: Complete replacement snapshot. At least one constraint is required.

aspect.description: Required delivery aspect as W:H; saved in reduced form.

clear.description: Set true to remove the saved kit. Mutually exclusive with brand.

verbs.result: {brand, cleared}

verbs.name: project.set_output_dir
verbs.description: Choose the FOLDER where exports + renders are written when a verb isn't given an explicit `path` (the UI 'Choose folder…' / agent control over the destination). The folder must already exist; it is canonicalized and becomes an allowed output-fence root. Empty/omitted `dir` clears the choice (back to <project>/exports). A workspace preference for the open session — NOT a timeline op, never replayed.

dir.description: Absolute path to an EXISTING folder for default-named exports. Empty/omitted = clear (revert to <project>/exports).

verbs.result: {dir} — the resolved output folder, or {dir:null, cleared:true} when cleared

verbs.name: library.list
verbs.description: List the global asset library (~/.shellx-cut/library/), filtered + sorted. The library holds media (video/audio/image) that lives ACROSS projects — added by the user or the agent, organized by folders + tags. READ-ONLY. Items LINK their original by src_path (default) or carry a content-addressed stored copy; the UI renders a blob thumbnail via /api/library-blob, else a type glyph.

tag.description: Filter to items carrying this tag (exact).

q.description: Case-insensitive name or tag substring filter.

sort.description: added (newest first, default) | name (asc) | recent (last-used) | uses (most-used).

collection.description: Server-side collection filter. missing computes backing-file existence before paging.

ids.description: Optional exact id-membership filter (maximum 500), intended for bounded cross-surface membership checks.

offset.description: Zero-based offset into the filtered, sorted result.

limit.description: Bounded page size. Defaults to 100 and may not exceed 500.

verbs.result: {items: [LibItem{id, type, name, src_path?, blob?, tags[], folder?, favorite?, added_ms, used_ms?, uses?, source, probe?:{duration_ms?,width?,height?,has_audio?}, media_ok:boolean}], folders:[string], tags:[string], total:int, offset:int, limit:int, next_offset?:int|null} — exactly one bounded page plus exact filtered total

verbs.name: library.add
verbs.description: Add a media file to the global library. Source = either path (a file on disk) OR asset (an asset id in the OPEN project → its source path). The file is ffprobe-VALIDATED (corrupt → rejected) and its KIND (video/audio/image) is derived from the probe, never a caller hint. By default the item LINKS the original (src_path; tiny disk). copy:true stores a content-addressed copy in library/blobs/<sha256>.<ext>. Idempotent by content hash (same file added twice = one item). source defaults to 'user' (set 'agent' when the agent curates).

path.description: Path to a media file to add (mutually exclusive with asset).

asset.description: An asset id in the open project to promote into the library (instead of path).

name.description: Display name (defaults to the file name).

tags.description: Tags to attach at add time.

copy.description: true = keep a managed copy in the Library blob store; false (default) = link the original by path.

verbs.result: {item: LibItem}

verbs.name: library.relink
verbs.description: Repair a missing LINKED Library source by pointing it at the SAME media bytes in a new filesystem location. The file is ffprobe-validated and content-hashed. Different content is rejected with conflict so the content-derived item id stays truthful. Managed copies are not relinked by this verb.

path.description: New absolute path to the same media bytes.

verbs.result: {item: LibItem} — the same item id and organization with its linked src_path repaired

verbs.name: library.remove
verbs.description: Remove a library item by id. A linked original is never touched; a copied blob is unlinked only when no other item references it (content dedup safe). Returns {removed:bool}.
verbs.result: {removed: bool}

verbs.name: library.move
verbs.description: Move a library item to a folder. Omit folder (or pass empty) to move it back to the root. Returns the updated {item}.
verbs.result: {item: LibItem}

verbs.name: library.tag
verbs.description: Replace a library item's tag set (the 'mark' gesture for assigning assets to project workflows). Returns the updated {item}.
verbs.result: {item: LibItem}

verbs.name: library.favorite
verbs.description: Pin/unpin a library item (favorites surface first in the UI). Returns the updated {item}.
verbs.result: {item: LibItem}

verbs.name: library.use
verbs.description: Bump a library item's recently-used timestamp + use count (drives the 'recent'/'uses' sorts). Called automatically by library.add_to_project; exposed for explicit telemetry. Returns the updated {item}.
verbs.result: {item: LibItem}

verbs.name: library.add_to_project
verbs.description: Import a library asset into the OPEN project — reuses media.import (hash/probe/proxy/transcribe/perception chain + auto-place when the timeline is empty) so the asset becomes a normal project asset (then place it with edit.insert). Also bumps the library use counter. Requires an open project; errors if the item's linked original has gone missing (re-add it, or use an item stored as a Library copy). Returns the media.import result (the new project asset).

id.description: The library item id to import.

verbs.result: the media.import result {asset_id, job_id, op, capture_manifest?} for the imported asset (probe lands async via the enrich_job)

verbs.name: library.folder_add
verbs.description: Create a library organization folder. No-op (added:false) if it already exists. Returns {added, folders}.
verbs.result: {added: bool, folders: [string]}

verbs.name: library.folder_rename
verbs.description: Rename a library folder and re-point every item filed under it. renamed:false if old is unknown or new is empty/taken. Returns {renamed, folders}.
verbs.result: {renamed: bool, folders: [string]}

verbs.name: library.folder_remove
verbs.description: Remove a library folder; its items are un-foldered (moved to root, NOT deleted). Returns {removed, folders}.
verbs.result: {removed: bool, folders: [string]}

verbs.name: comment.add
verbs.description: Append a timecoded REVIEW COMMENT. Anchors review feedback at a timeline position (at_ms, optional end_ms for a range) with a free-text note; status starts 'open'. When a clip exists under at_ms, the stored comment also carries anchor:{track_id,clip_id,offset_ms} so the UI/agents can resolve it after upstream ripple edits and badge it stale if the clip is removed. A review-metadata op (in the op-log for receipts + replay, but NOT a timeline edit / not in the undo stack). The agent later drafts a concrete change for it (comment.draft) which is reviewed + applied (comment.apply). author defaults to 'client'.

at_ms.description: Timeline anchor, ms

end_ms.description: End of a range comment (ms); omit for a point comment

verbs.result: {comment: {id, at_ms, end_ms?, anchor?:{track_id,clip_id,offset_ms}, text, author, status, ts}}; one op appended

verbs.name: comment.export
verbs.description: Export a PORTABLE OFFLINE REVIEW PACKAGE for the latest persisted render receipt: a standalone HTML reviewer, a receipt-verified copy of the rendered media, and a machine-readable manifest. The receipt output must be inside an authorized export folder — the project's exports subtree, CUTD_OUTPUTS_DIR, or the folder chosen with project.set_output_dir — which is where the engine is allowed to deliver a render in the first place; this prevents a tampered receipt from turning the export route into an arbitrary-file reader. The reviewer plays the copied render, accepts timecoded notes without a server, and downloads shellx-cut/review-feedback/1 JSON for comment.import. By default no render-affecting op may follow the receipt (later comment/preset/name metadata is harmless), so reviewers never receive a stale cut. Read-only (no op).

path.description: Optional fenced .html output path. The media and manifest are written beside it. Default exports/review_<render_id>.html.

allow_stale.description: Explicitly export an older latest render even when the project changed after it. The package remains bound to the receipt's source_op_id and reports stale:true.

verbs.result: {path, manifest_path, media_path, render_id, source_op_id, render_hash, stale}; no op

verbs.name: comment.import
verbs.description: Import shellx-cut/review-feedback/1 JSON downloaded by a portable review package. Validates the schema, size/count/text/time bounds, source op, render id, and render hash against the saved local receipt, then appends every note ATOMICALLY as one replay-safe review-metadata op. Each imported comment carries review_source:{source_op_id,render_id,render_hash}. Later comment/preset/name metadata does not stale unchanged rendered bytes; any later render-affecting op does, and requires allow_stale:true plus a rationale.

path.description: Path to a shellx-cut/review-feedback/1 JSON file (max 2 MiB, 1-500 comments).

allow_stale.description: Explicitly import feedback against an older reviewed render. Requires rationale.

rationale.description: Audit reason; required when allow_stale imports feedback against an older project head.

verbs.result: {comments, count, source_op_id, render_id, reviewed_project, current_project, stale}; one atomic comment.import op appended

verbs.name: comment.list
verbs.description: List review comments, optionally filtered by lifecycle status. Read-only (no op). New comments may include anchor:{track_id,clip_id,offset_ms}; resolve that against current project.state tracks to follow the clip after ripple edits, and treat a missing clip as a stale/orphaned note.

status.description: Filter to this status; omit for all

verbs.result: {comments: [...], count}

verbs.name: comment.resolve
verbs.description: Set a comment's lifecycle status: 'addressed' (its drafted change was applied), 'dismissed' (won't act on it), or back to 'open'. A review-metadata op.
verbs.result: {comment}; one op appended

verbs.name: comment.draft
verbs.description: Ask the drafting agent (the verify.judge claude-CLI ladder, reused) to propose a concrete change set for an OPEN review comment — a sequence of editor verb calls that addresses it, given the timeline + transcript context + the verb catalog. The proposal is STORED on the comment for review (comment.draft does NOT apply it; comment.apply executes it after review). Honest backend semantics like verify.judge: a missing/not-logged-in CLI returns status 'not_run', a run that fails returns 'error', and NO draft is stored in either case (never a fabricated edit). The proposed verbs are validated against the real registry (unknown/non-actionable verbs flagged in draft.validation).

comment_id.description: Comment id (cmN) from comment.list — must be an existing comment

verbs.result: {comment_id, status: completed|not_run|error, draft?: {verbs:[{verb,args}], rationale, confidence, validation, backend}}; one op appended on success

verbs.name: comment.apply
verbs.description: EXECUTE a comment's drafted change. Dispatches each verb in the comment's draft as a real op carrying the comment as its rationale (the receipt linking the edit to the comment), wrapped in an AUTO-CHECKPOINT so the whole apply is revertible in one step (project.revert{to: the returned checkpoint}). Returns the before/after project.diff — the review artifact — and marks the comment 'addressed'. Stops on the FIRST failing verb and hands back the checkpoint to revert the partial apply (a half-applied draft is never left silently). Requires the comment to have a draft (run comment.draft first); a no-op draft (empty verbs) is refused — dismiss the comment instead.

comment_id.description: Comment id (cmN) — must have a draft from comment.draft

verbs.result: {comment_id, status: addressed|failed, applied:[{verb,ok,result,error}], diff, checkpoint, revert_hint}; appends a checkpoint + the drafted ops + a comment.resolve

verbs.name: media.import
verbs.description: Import a media file as an asset: hashes it, registers it as an op, and kicks the probe→auto-place import chain; proxy/filmstrip and transcribe/perception run as SEPARATE background jobs (proxy_job + enrich_job). Returns immediately. Still images (PNG/JPEG/…) are accepted: probe reports kind=image with no duration, the chain stops after probe (proxy/transcribe/perception skipped — named in the job result), and placement requires edit.insert{duration_ms}. CAPTURE MANIFEST: pass capture_manifest (path to a shellx-cut/capture-manifest/1 JSON written by the recording agent, resolved beside the imported media), or drop it beside the media as <stem>.capture.json — auto-discovered with an in-band warning. Each manifest event becomes a `capture:<type>` marker op (system actor, review-rail visible) with the FULL event payload — data, confidence tag, provenance — preserved in the marker note; events resolve time via at_ms (media time, the contract default) → range_ms[0] (spans mark their start) → utc mapped through recording.clock_map (piecewise-linear, clamped at the anchored span's edges). Markers are created ONLY when this import is auto-placed as the timeline (media time == timeline time); otherwise the job result says so (markers are timeline-absolute). Markers remain confidence-tagged claims from the capture agent and never enter RenderReceipt facts.

path.description: Path to the media file to import

capture_manifest.description: Path to a shellx-cut/capture-manifest/1 JSON, resolved beside the imported media and rejected if it escapes that directory. Omit to auto-discover <stem>.capture.json beside the media (warned in-band). Explicit-path errors are hard; a malformed auto-discovered sidecar degrades to a warning.

proxy.description: Generate the 960x540 editing proxy in the import chain (default true). Set false for HEAVY files (large FHD / multi-GB raw) to import INSTANTLY instead of blocking minutes on the transcode: the asset stays usable (transcript edits + composed-frame poster scrub from the source), the filmstrip is skipped, and the FINAL RENDER USES THE SOURCE — so output quality is unaffected. Smooth proxy <video> playback is unavailable until/unless a proxy is built.

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {asset_id, job_id, capture_manifest?: {path, events}} — watch job_progress events or poll jobs.status; the chain job result carries capture_manifest.{markers_created, events_skipped, skipped[], note}

verbs.name: media.remove
verbs.description: Drop an imported asset from the OPEN project — the inverse of media.import and the file-removal half of project cleanup (project.delete removes projects). Removes the assets[<id>] record via a recorded, REPLAY-SAFE media.remove op and unlinks regenerable derived files. Normal user-imported source media is NEVER touched. A project-owned generated source that is a direct child of canonical assets/generated is deleted with its provenance sidecar only after the last asset reference is removed. SAFE DEFAULT: refuses with CONFLICT while any timeline clip still references the asset. Asset removal itself is not timeline-undoable; re-import to restore. Requires an open project.

asset.description: Asset id (e.g. "a1") to remove from the open project. List ids via project.state (project.assets).

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {removed:true,asset,source_kept:<ordinary source path or null>,source_deleted:boolean,freed:[...]} — source_deleted is true only for a last-reference project-owned assets/generated file (its provenance sidecar is also freed); ordinary imported sources are always kept

verbs.name: media.relink
verbs.description: Repoint an imported asset at a new source file — the recovery verb for OFFLINE media (source moved, renamed, or restored elsewhere). Two modes decided by content hash: SAME hash = the file merely moved, pure repath and every derived artifact (probe/proxy/filmstrip/transcript/perception) is KEPT; NEW hash = different content, derived state is cleared and regenerated via the same import chain a fresh media.import runs (result carries the chain job_id — poll jobs.status), while every timeline clip keeps referencing the same asset id (no re-editing needed). Refuses INVALID_ARGS on a KIND mismatch (e.g. relinking a video asset to an audio file — clips assume the kind; import a new asset + edit.replace instead). WARNS (code relink_shorter_than_used) when the new file is shorter than the furthest source point used by any clip — re-trim those clips or renders come up short. REPLAY-SAFE metadata op off the undo cursor (relink back to the old path to restore). Requires an open project. media.check lists which assets are offline.

asset.description: Asset id (e.g. "a1") to repoint. List ids via project.state (project.assets); media.check flags the offline ones.

path.description: Absolute path to the new source media file (must exist and be readable).

verbs.result: {asset, path, old_path, hash_changed, derived_cleared, freed: [<stale derived files unlinked>], job_id?: <import-chain job when content changed>} — NOT_FOUND if the asset id or target path is unknown, INVALID_ARGS on kind mismatch; warning relink_shorter_than_used when clips use source beyond the new duration

verbs.name: media.check
verbs.description: Read-only OFFLINE-media report: for every imported asset (or one, with {asset}), does its SOURCE file currently exist on disk, and how many timeline clips reference it. Existence is computed from the filesystem at call time — never persisted — so the answer cannot go stale (a moved file shows offline immediately; a restored file shows online immediately). Run before render/export to catch missing media early (render fails with NOT_FOUND on the first offline asset it needs); fix offline assets via media.relink {asset, path} or by restoring the file at its recorded path. The UI's asset tray polls this for offline badges. Requires an open project.

asset.description: Check just this asset id; omit to check every asset in the project.

verbs.result: {count, offline_count, assets: [{asset, path, exists, modified_ms?: <source file Unix epoch ms>, referenced: <number of timeline clips using it>}]} — NOT_FOUND when a requested asset id is unknown

verbs.name: media.bin_save
verbs.description: Save (upsert) a SMART BIN — a NAMED SAVED SEARCH over the project's asset tray (a standard saved-search convention). Membership is COMPUTED at list time (media.bin_list) from the query, never stored, so a bin can't go stale as assets are imported/removed or placed/unplaced. Criteria are AND-combined: media type, name text, unused/used, minimum resolution, missing/offline state, and source modified-time range. At least ONE criterion is required (a bin matching everything is just the tray — refused). Name-keyed: a re-save under the same name REPLACES the query. Replay-safe non-timeline metadata op (the grade.save pattern, off the undo cursor); media.bin_delete removes. The Assets tray renders bins as filter chips with live counts.

kind.description: Only assets of this probe kind.

text.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the source file's basename.

unused.description: true = only assets NOT referenced by any timeline clip (find unused media); false = only assets ON the timeline.

min_width.description: Minimum probed source width in pixels. Assets without probe metadata do not match.

min_height.description: Minimum probed source height in pixels. Assets without probe metadata do not match.

offline.description: true = only missing/offline source files; false = only source files currently present on disk.

modified_after_ms.description: Inclusive lower bound for source file modification time in Unix epoch milliseconds.

modified_before_ms.description: Inclusive upper bound for source file modification time in Unix epoch milliseconds.

verbs.result: {bin: {name, kind?, text?, unused?, min_width?, min_height?, offline?, modified_after_ms?, modified_before_ms?}, replaced: <true when an existing bin of that name was overwritten>} — invalid_args on an empty name, no criteria, invalid resolution/date range, or an unknown kind

verbs.name: media.bin_delete
verbs.description: Delete a smart bin by name (see media.bin_save). Replay-safe metadata op. The assets the bin matched are untouched — a bin is only a saved search.

name.description: Bin name to delete (media.bin_list shows them).

verbs.result: {deleted: <name>} — NOT_FOUND when no bin carries the name

verbs.name: media.bin_list
verbs.description: Read-only: every smart bin with its LIVE membership — matching asset ids computed against the current tray, timeline usage, source-file availability, source resolution, and modified times at call time (never cached). Use to browse saved searches or to fetch 'unused media' / 'missing media' / '4K clips' style groupings for further edits.
verbs.result: {count, bins: [{name, kind?, text?, unused?, min_width?, min_height?, offline?, modified_after_ms?, modified_before_ms?, matches: [asset ids], match_count}]}

verbs.name: media.probe
verbs.description: Probe an asset (ffprobe) and store the normalized result on the asset. Synchronous (probing is fast).

asset.description: Asset id

verbs.result: MediaProbe {kind: video|audio|image, duration_ms? (absent for stills), width?, height?, fps?, has_audio, audio_rate?, format, raw}

verbs.name: media.waveform
verbs.description: Per-bucket audio peaks (abs-max amplitude, 0..1, left->right in time) for the timeline waveform. Synchronous + deterministic; the decode rate is bounded by the probed duration so memory stays small for any clip length. Errors when the asset has no audio stream.

buckets.description: Number of peak buckets to return (default 1000).

verbs.result: {asset, bucket_count, peaks:[float 0..1], source_ms, sample_rate} — peaks left-to-right in time

verbs.name: media.filmstrip
verbs.description: Build a timeline THUMBNAIL TILE for a video asset from its proxy — a horizontal row of evenly-spaced frames. TWO modes: (1) WHOLE-ASSET (no range_ms) = the base strip over [0,duration], stored on the asset (field `filmstrip`), idempotent, built automatically in the import chain after the proxy step; the UI slices it per clip by the linear fraction t/duration. (2) WINDOWED / ZOOM (range_ms given) = sample just that SOURCE sub-range at `count` frames — the per-zoom density path: the UI requests exactly the frames visible for a clip at the current zoom (≈1 thumb per fixed pixel width), so as you zoom in the window shrinks and density rises, approaching per-frame at sub-second zoom; ephemeral (NOT stored on the asset), returns {thumbs, range_ms, count, h}. Cost is bounded because only the visible window is ever sampled. Video assets WITH a proxy only.

asset.description: Asset id (must be a video asset with a built proxy)

range_ms.description: WINDOWED mode: [start_ms, end_ms) in the asset's own SOURCE time — sample just this window (the visible clip range at the current zoom) instead of the whole asset. Clamped to [0, duration). Omit for the whole-asset base strip.

count.description: WINDOWED mode: number of frames tiled across the window (≈1 per fixed pixel width of the visible clip). Clamped to [12,160] server-side. Default 12.

h.description: WINDOWED mode: thumbnail height in px. Default 80.

verbs.result: WHOLE-ASSET: {filmstrip} — relative path filmstrip/<id>.jpg (served at /filmstrip/<id>.jpg). WINDOWED: {thumbs, range_ms, count, h} — thumbs = filmstrip/<id>_w<t0>-<t1>_<count>x<h>.jpg, same /filmstrip/ route.

verbs.name: media.transcribe
verbs.description: Run word-level transcription on an asset (job, returns {job_id}). Uses the active STT model from system.set_stt_model: Parakeet v3 by default, Canary-1B-v2 + MMS_FA for smaller-language accuracy, or Whisper large-v3 fallback. Writes receipts/<asset>.words.json and links it on the asset.

model.description: Legacy per-call model override. Prefer system.set_stt_model so the Environment panel, doctor card, and agents agree on the active model.

verbs.result: {job_id} — completion event carries the transcript summary

verbs.name: media.perception
verbs.description: Full instrument run on an asset (words, silences, scenes, beats, loudness) → receipts/<asset>.perception.json (job, returns {job_id}). Cached by asset hash.
verbs.result: {job_id} — completion event carries the PerceptionReport path

verbs.name: media.diarize
verbs.description: SPEAKER DIARIZATION ('who spoke when') on an asset as a background job (returns {job_id}) — the heavier, separately-provisioned sibling of media.transcribe. Extracts the asset's audio to 16 kHz mono and POSTs it to the diarization service (NVIDIA Sortformer streaming v2, CC-BY-4.0, ≤4 speakers; arrival-order labels S1..Sn), then writes the normalized speaker turns into receipts/<asset>.perception.json as `speaker_turns` AND labels each transcript word with the speaker of the turn it overlaps MOST in time (`WordSpan.speaker`, refreshed into receipts/<asset>.words.json) — so transcript.get / transcript.timeline / captions are speaker-labeled and edit.multicam_switch / audio.dub can key by speaker identity. Also writes receipts/<asset>.diarize.json. If the asset has no transcript yet, the turns are still recorded (words get labeled on the next media.transcribe + media.diarize). Endpoint: CUT_DIARIZE_ENDPOINT (default http://127.0.0.1:9002; set it before launch when the service uses a custom address). The runtime absent / the service unreachable or still loading → an actionable SETUP error (like media.index), never faked turns.

max_speakers.description: Advisory cap — keep only the N most-talkative speakers (Sortformer itself hard-caps at 4). Default: the service's own (4).

verbs.result: {job_id} — completion event carries {diarization (receipt path), backend, model, num_speakers, n_turns, labeled_words, turns:[{start_ms,end_ms,speaker}]}

verbs.name: media.index_status
verbs.description: Read VISUAL-SEARCH index status for the current project without running the SigLIP2 indexer. Used by the Find moment UI and agents to tell which imported assets already have persisted embeddings under embeddings/<asset>.json after reopening a project. Model/runtime-free: reports existing indexes only; use media.index to build one.

asset.description: Optional imported asset id to inspect. Omit to list every indexed asset in the open project.

verbs.result: {count, assets:[{asset, indexed_frames, dim, model, path}]}

verbs.name: media.index
verbs.description: Build the VISUAL-SEARCH index for an asset : sample its frames at `fps` and embed each with the SigLIP2 image encoder → embeddings/<asset>.json, so media.search can then find MOMENTS by content ('the slide with the chart'). OPTIONAL + fetch-on-consent (the matte pattern): the indexer needs the perception venv (onnxruntime) + a SigLIP2 ONNX model. When that runtime is ABSENT the verb returns an actionable SETUP error (core editing + search of an already-built index work without re-indexing). Requires an open project.

asset.description: The imported asset id to index.

fps.description: Frames per second to sample for embedding (default 1.0).

verbs.result: {asset, indexed_frames, dim, model, path}

verbs.name: media.search
verbs.description: ON-DEVICE VISUAL SEARCH: find the MOMENTS in indexed clips that match a query, by matching a query embedding against the per-frame SigLIP2 image embeddings (media.index) and merging the best adjacent frames into time RANGES. Pass `query` text (embedded live by the SigLIP2 TEXT encoder through the perception runtime — errors with a setup pointer only when that runtime is absent) OR `query_vector` (an already-embedded query — the advanced/agent path, usable without the runtime). `asset` narrows to one clip; omitted searches every indexed asset. Returns ranked {asset, start_ms, end_ms, peak_ms, score}. Requires an open project; errors if nothing is indexed yet (run media.index first). Integration coverage verifies that a text query resolves the matching frame range through real SigLIP2 image and text embeddings.

query.description: A natural-language query (needs the SigLIP2 text encoder). Use `query_vector` to search without the model.

query_vector.description: An already-embedded query vector (same dim as the index) — searches without needing the text encoder.

asset.description: Limit the search to one asset's index; omit to search all indexed assets.

top_k.description: How many ranked moments to return (default 8).

max_gap_ms.description: Adjacent matching frames within this gap merge into one moment (default 2000).

verbs.result: {count, hits: [{asset, start_ms, end_ms, peak_ms, score}]}

verbs.name: effects.list
verbs.description: List the effects-as-data CATALOG : every `edit.effect` effect with its track (video/audio), one-line description, overlay-only flag, and parameter schema (name, type number|color, min/max/default, required). A pure READ (no project needed) so a UI or agent can DISCOVER the available effects + their parameters without hardcoding. Generated from the in-house catalog (drift-guarded against the ClipEffect enum), so it never drifts from what edit.effect accepts. (The render LOWERING stays native Rust to keep every existing effect byte-identical — this registry is the discovery/validation spine beside it.)
verbs.result: {count, effects: [{key, track, description, overlay_only, params: [{name, kind, min?, max?, default?, required}]}]}

verbs.name: transitions.list
verbs.description: List the transitions-as-data CATALOG : every `edit.crossfade` VIDEO-transition style (ffmpeg `xfade`) with its family (dissolve/wipe/slide/smooth/cover/reveal/shape/slice/diagonal/squeeze/zoom/wind), motion direction where meaningful, and a one-line description of the seam. A pure READ (no project needed) so a UI or agent can DISCOVER and pick a transition by look/direction without hardcoding names. Generated from the in-house catalog (drift-guarded against the canonical transition set), so it never drifts from what edit.crossfade {transition} accepts. Also returns the distinct `categories` for grouped UI. (Audio always crossfades smoothly under any video style; this is the VIDEO seam look.)
verbs.result: {count, categories: [string], transitions: [{name, category, direction?, description}]}

verbs.name: jobs.status
verbs.description: Status of one background job (probe/proxy/transcribe/perception/render/judge). jobs domain replaces media.status.
verbs.result: JobRecord {job_id, kind, state: queued|running|done|failed, completion?: success|done_with_warnings, outcome?: succeeded|failed|cancelled|interrupted|superseded, outcome_reason?: completed|completed_with_warnings|true_failure|user_cancelled|project_switch_cancelled|restart_interrupted|superseded, progress 0..1, message?, queue?:{resource,max_running}, waiting_on?:{job_id,kind}, error?, result?}. message is the latest durable human-readable progress or terminal phase; it is absent on queued/legacy records until a worker reports one. queue is present only while a limited job waits for the named shared local resource and states its concurrency capacity; it clears when the slot is acquired or the job becomes terminal. waiting_on is present only while an orchestrator awaits the named active child and is relationship evidence, not a retry promise. state remains backward-compatible; outcome/outcome_reason explain terminal cause and are absent on legacy persisted records. completion is present on newly completed jobs; done_with_warnings means the result is usable but partial and its result.warnings must be inspected.

verbs.name: jobs.list
verbs.description: All job records of this server run, newest first (status bar + agent overview). Active records retain their latest human-readable message so a reconnect can restore the current phase without waiting for another progress event.
verbs.result: {jobs: JobRecord[], persistence_notices: [{code:'job_record_quarantined',record,message,quarantine}]}. persistence_notices is empty unless project recovery quarantined malformed job JSON; quarantine is relative to the project's jobs directory.

verbs.name: jobs.cancel
verbs.description: Cancel one active background job from this server run. state remains failed with code job_cancelled for client compatibility, while jobs.status records outcome:cancelled and outcome_reason:user_cancelled. Cancellation waits for tracked blocking workers and their synchronous child processes to finish; if the bounded drain period expires, job_cancel_pending tells the caller to wait and retry instead of falsely claiming the worker stopped. Already-finished, recovered, or unknown jobs are rejected with structured errors.
verbs.result: {job_id, cancelled:true}

verbs.name: edit.split
verbs.description: Split the clip under the given timeline position on a track into two clips. at_ms is EDITORIAL time (the cumulative clip-duration sum) — after a crossfade shortens the realized timeline, render/playhead positions diverge from it.

group_id.description: Undo-grouping tag (optional). Ops in ONE logical user action (a linked A/V split cuts the video clip + its audio sibling at the same editorial position) pass the same tag so the undo cursor steps over the whole group in one Ctrl+Z. Omit for a standalone split. Ignored by replay/effects beyond the cursor.

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {clip_ids: [left, right]} — both resulting clip ids; one op appended

verbs.name: edit.cut_to_beat
verbs.description: Cut/align clips to MUSIC BEATS — a beat-synced montage where each clip change lands on a beat. BEAT SOURCE (v1): the beat:N markers audio.add_music{beat_markers:true} surfaces from the bed asset's perception BeatGrid (markers with label 'beat', at_ms = the beat's timeline position). No beat markers in scope → actionable error pointing at audio.add_music (transcript-onset / downbeat detection are documented future sources). every_n (default 1) uses every Nth beat (2 = every 2nd, 4 = every bar) for slower cutting; range_ms limits the span. mode 'split' (default): split the track (default the base video track) at each selected beat inside its content, so every cut lands on a beat (the montage skeleton to fill/reorder); beats on an existing cut (±epsilon) or in a gap are skipped — no slivers, idempotent. mode 'snap': ROLL each existing cut boundary to the nearest beat within max_snap_ms (trims the left clip's out-edge + right clip's in-edge by the same delta), locking an assembled sequence to the grid without crossing neighbours or shifting downstream timing; a roll lacking source headroom is skipped. v1 lowers to individual replay-safe edit.split/edit.trim ops (one per cut/edge, like edit.split_at_scenes).

track.description: Track to cut/align (default: the base video track).

mode.description: split (default) = cut at each beat; snap = roll existing cut boundaries onto beats.

every_n.description: Use every Nth beat (default 1). 2 = every 2nd beat, 4 = every bar (slower cutting).

range_ms.description: Limit the cut/align span to [start, end) timeline ms.

max_snap_ms.description: snap mode: max ms a cut boundary may travel to reach a beat (default 120).

verbs.result: {mode, track, cuts:[at_ms], beats_used, every_n, beats_available, moves?:[{from,to}]} — one edit.split (split) or edit.trim (snap) op per cut/edge; no beat markers → error; no clips in range → clean no-op (cuts:[])

verbs.name: edit.split_at_scenes
verbs.description: Split the base clip at the asset's detected SCENE boundaries (turns a multi-shot screen-demo/montage into editable shots). Scene cuts come from the perception 'scenes' instrument (source time), mapped to timeline via the clip carrying each; boundary/out-of-clip positions are skipped. min_shot_ms drops cuts that would make a shot shorter than that. One edit.split op per split.

track.description: Target video track (default: first video track).

min_shot_ms.description: Drop cuts that would make a shot shorter than this (default 500).

verbs.result: {asset, track, scene_cuts, splits} — splits = edit.split ops appended

verbs.name: edit.mark_scenes
verbs.description: Add a marker at each detected SCENE boundary on the timeline (navigate instead of cut; complements edit.split_at_scenes). Composes with export.chapters for automatic chapter generation from scenes. One edit.add_marker op per scene boundary.

track.description: Target video track (default: first video track).

label_prefix.description: Marker label prefix (default "Scene"); markers are "<prefix> N".

verbs.result: {asset, scene_cuts, markers_added}

verbs.name: edit.trim_edges
verbs.description: Top-and-tail: remove leading + trailing DEAD AIR (before the first spoken word / after the last) while preserving internal pacing — unlike transcript.remove_silences which removes every silence. Anchors to SPEECH (word timings via the EDL), leaving keep_pad_ms of breath each side. The dedicated fix for the silence_at_edges render check. Silent footage = honest no-op.

keep_pad_ms.description: Breath left before first / after last speech (default 200).

min_trim_ms.description: Don't trim an edge smaller than this (default 250).

verbs.result: {leading_trimmed_ms, trailing_trimmed_ms, first_speech_ms?, last_speech_ms?, note?}

verbs.name: edit.ripple_delete
verbs.description: Remove a timeline range. One track, or ALL tracks when track is omitted (keeps AV in sync). ripple selects the NLE edit kind: ripple=true (DEFAULT, the older behavior — omitting it replays byte-identical) CLOSES the gap (extract: later content shifts left, captions/markers/duck-windows remap); ripple=false LEAVES a gap of equal length where the content was (LIFT: nothing downstream moves, captions/markers/duck-windows stay put — the 'remove this clip, keep everyone else's timing' edit).

track.description: Omit to ripple every track

ripple.description: true (default) = close the gap (extract); false = leave a gap (lift). Omitting it replays as close-gap (byte-identical to older logs).

group_id.description: Undo-grouping tag (optional). Ops in ONE logical user action (a linked A/V delete/cut deletes the video + its audio sibling) pass the same tag so the undo cursor steps over the whole group in one Ctrl+Z. Omit for a standalone edit. Ignored by replay/effects beyond the cursor.

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {removed_ms, tracks, ripple} — the resolved edit kind; one op appended with per-track effects

verbs.name: edit.trim
verbs.description: Adjust a clip's source in/out points (either or both); the timeline ripples to the new duration. linked defaults true for live calls: when the clip has one exact imported A/V counterpart (opposite kind, same asset/source range/timeline span), both clips trim atomically so video and audio stay aligned; linked:false deliberately trims one clip. Old logged trims without linked lowering replay with their historical one-clip behavior.

clip.description: Clip id

linked.description: Trim one exact inferred A/V counterpart in the same atomic action. Set false for a deliberate independent trim.

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {clip, src_in_ms, src_out_ms, linked, linked_clip, linked_track} — the new source range and inferred counterpart (or null); one op appended

verbs.name: edit.move
verbs.description: Move a clip to a (possibly different) track at a timeline position. Gap-fills the source slot (the source track does NOT ripple) and splices into the destination. linked defaults true for live calls: when the clip has one exact imported A/V counterpart (opposite kind, same asset/source range/timeline span), both clips move atomically and one undo restores both; linked:false deliberately moves one clip. ripple false (default) leaves unrelated tracks fixed; true opens an AV-sync gap in every OTHER video/audio track after both linked destinations are populated and remaps captions/markers/duck-windows. Old logged moves without linked lowering replay with their historical one-clip behavior.

ripple.description: false (default) = move the selected clip and its exact linked counterpart without shifting unrelated tracks; true = also open time on every other media track and remap captions/markers/duck-windows.

linked.description: Move one exact inferred A/V counterpart in the same atomic action. Set false for a deliberate independent move.

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {clip, track, at_ms, ripple, linked, linked_clip, linked_track, rippled_tracks} — final placement, resolved link/ripple modes, inferred counterpart (or null), and unrelated tracks that received the gap; one op appended

verbs.name: edit.insert
verbs.description: Insert an asset as a new clip on a track at a timeline position; later clips on that track shift right. src_range_ms selects a sub-range of the asset (defaults to full duration). STILL IMAGES (probe kind=image) have no intrinsic duration: pass duration_ms instead (REQUIRED for images; video tracks only) — the render loops the still for the clip duration, conformed to project geometry. RIPPLE MATRIX (default chosen by TARGET track; explicit `ripple` always wins): BASE track target (the first video track with clips — the renderer's base-canvas rule — or the first audio track with clips; positional first of the kind when all are empty) → default ripple=TRUE: a gap of the inserted duration is spliced into every OTHER video/audio track at at_ms (razor-across-tracks; tracks ending at/before at_ms are untouched), caption ranges + duck gain-windows remap edge-wise, markers at/after at_ms shift right by the inserted duration — AV sync and overlay/caption/marker alignment preserved (mirror of ripple_delete's all-tracks form). OVERLAY/EXTRA track target (any later video track = PiP overlay; any later audio track = music/SFX bed) → default ripple=FALSE: overlays float above the base, nothing else moves. ripple=false on a base track is the deliberate overlay/replace opt-out (siblings + markers stay put, consistent with single-track ripple_delete). In BOTH modes the target track's own duck windows follow its shifted content. The RESOLVED ripple value is recorded explicitly on the op (ops are self-contained; ops logged before this flag replay as ripple=false).

duration_ms.description: Clip duration for STILL-IMAGE assets (which have no intrinsic duration). Invalid for timed media (use src_range_ms). Mutually exclusive with src_range_ms.

ripple.description: Shift sibling tracks' content after at_ms by the inserted duration (gap-insert) + remap captions/duck-windows/markers. OMITTED = resolved from the target track: base video/audio track → true (AV sync preserved), overlay/extra track → false (overlays float). See the ripple matrix in the verb description.

group_id.description: Undo-grouping tag (optional). A linked A/V paste inserts the video + its linked audio as TWO ops sharing this tag, so one Ctrl+Z undoes the whole paste. Omit for a standalone insert. Ignored by replay/effects beyond the cursor.

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {clip_id, ripple, rippled_tracks} — the new clip, the RESOLVED ripple mode, and the sibling tracks that received the gap; one op appended

verbs.name: edit.detach_audio
verbs.description: Extract (PROMOTE) a video clip's audio onto its own editable audio track -- the 'Detach Audio' affordance, reframed for this engine. MODEL NOTE: the renderer mixes audio from AUDIO tracks ONLY, so a video's audio normally lives as a SEPARATE audio-track clip (the auto-place v1/a1t mirror). Exact sibling pairs are inferred as linked for edit.move by default; pass linked:false when an independent J/L-style offset is deliberate. This verb still means EXTRACT, not unlink: when no sibling audio clip exists it creates one at the video's timeline start; when one already exists it returns a clean informational no-op {detached:false}. Lowers to ONE replay-safe edit.insert (preceded by edit.add_track only when the project has no audio track). v1 refuses a retimed (speed != 1) clip because normal-speed extracted audio would desync the stretched video.

clip.description: Id of the VIDEO-track media clip whose audio to extract.

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {detached, audio_clip?, audio_track?, at_ms?, src_range_ms?, added_to_render?, reason?} -- detached:true extracted the audio onto audio_track as the new audio_clip (added_to_render:true: it was absent before); detached:false means the audio was already on its own track (reason + the existing audio_clip). One edit.insert op (plus an edit.add_track only when no audio track existed).

verbs.name: edit.duplicate
verbs.description: Duplicate a clip (the universal NLE Ctrl+D / 'Duplicate'): copy a clip and place the copy IMMEDIATELY AFTER it on the SAME track, rippling the rest like a normal insert. The copy carries the SAME asset + source range AND ALL per-clip attributes -- effects, gain_db, transform, crop, fade, speed, speed_ramp, grade, matte, mask (redact), reverse, freeze, animation, keyframes, eq, stabilize -- i.e. the whole clip minus its id (a TRUE copy, unlike edit.paste which makes a pristine clip). The clone's crossfade-IN is reset to a hard cut (a crossfade is a property of the ORIGINAL left-neighbour boundary, not the clip's content -- the same rule split's right half uses). LINKED AUDIO: when the source is a muxed VIDEO clip whose audio rides a sibling AUDIO clip (same asset + same timeline start -- the auto-place / linked-insert signature), that sibling is duplicated too so the A/V pair stays aligned; both halves go ripple:false (the aligned-pair pattern) and share one undo group. A LONE clip resolves its ripple from the host track like edit.insert (base track -> sibling AV-sync gap, overlay/extra -> float). Each half lowers to ONE replay-safe edit.duplicate core op (a clone-by-reference whose new id is pinned). Works on a retimed/ramped clip (the whole clip is copied at a boundary -- no timeline->source split). v1 copies the whole clip (no sub-range, no overwrite).

clip.description: Id of the media clip to duplicate (project.state lists clips).

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {source_clip, new_clip, track, at_ms, linked_audio?} -- new_clip is the cloned clip's id, placed on `track` at `at_ms` (immediately after the source). linked_audio is non-null when a muxed video clip's sibling audio was duplicated too: {source_clip, new_clip, track}. One edit.duplicate op (two, grouped, when linked audio is duplicated).

verbs.name: edit.nest
verbs.description: Collapse a CONTIGUOUS run of clips on ONE track into a single NEST / COMPOUND CLIP (a nested compound clip): a group of clips grouped into one nested sub-timeline that acts as a single clip on the parent track. The selected `clips` (which must be MEDIA clips, all on the SAME track, forming a CONTIGUOUS run of adjacent clips with NOTHING -- no gap, no caption -- between them) MOVE off the parent track into a new sub-timeline stored on the project (project.state shows it under `nests`), rebased so the first starts at sub-time 0, with EVERY per-clip attribute preserved (grade, effects, fade, speed, timing). They are REPLACED in place by a SINGLE nest clip occupying their combined [at_ms, at_ms+span) range, so the parent timeline LENGTH is unchanged. The nest clip is marked by its `nest` field (= the new nest id) and its `asset` references the same nest id (its source IS the nest). RENDER = BAKE: at render time the server renders the nest's sub-timeline to a content-addressed cache file (reusing the render.final path, cached by sub-timeline hash so it re-renders only when the nest changes) and feeds that baked file in as the nest clip's source -- the main renderer is nest-blind, so a project with no nest renders byte-identical. Replay-safe: ONE op (the nest clip id is pinned, the nest id is deterministic). EDGE CASES (documented): a crossfade INTO the first nested clip is dropped (the nest clip hard-cuts from its predecessor, like edit.duplicate); v1 nests a SINGLE track's run, so a base-video run's linked audio on a separate track is NOT pulled in (it stays on the parent); nesting a clip that is already a nest is refused (no nest-of-nest). v1 scope is CREATE + RENDER -- editing INSIDE a nest after creation is a documented follow-up.

clips.description: Ids of the clips to collapse into the nest -- a contiguous run of MEDIA clips on ONE track (project.state lists clips). Order does not matter; they are nested in track order.

name.description: Optional human label for the nest (shown in project.state under nests).

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {clip_id, nest_id, track, at_ms, span_ms, nested_clips} -- clip_id is the single nest clip that replaced the run on `track` (spanning [at_ms, at_ms+span_ms)); nest_id is the new sub-timeline (in project.nests) holding nested_clips. One replay-safe edit.nest op.

verbs.name: edit.replace
verbs.description: The 3-point REPLACE EDIT: swap the clip at `target_clip`'s timeline slot with new source footage while PRESERVING the target's id, timeline position, and slot duration. The source is given as either an imported `asset` or an existing `source_clip` (its asset + default source window); `source_in_ms`/`source_out_ms` set/override the source in/out. The replacement keeps the target clip's LOOK (effects, grade, transform, crop, fade, gain, eq, mask, matte, stabilize, reverse, transitions, keyframes, animation) and plays at NORMAL speed (1.0); the three source-timing fields tied to the OLD footage -- constant speed, speed_ramp, freeze -- are RESET (use edit.fit_to_fill to speed-match a slot instead). SLOT FILL + CLAMP: at normal speed the replacement uses [source_in, source_in+slot) of source, so it fills the slot exactly; if the chosen source window is SHORTER than the slot (insufficient media), the replacement is clamped and the REMAINDER of the slot is left as a gap (black/silence) -- a clamp-and-pad, NOT a ripple -- so the slot's duration and ALL downstream timing are preserved exactly (gap_ms in the receipt reports the pad). LINKED AUDIO (link_audio, default true): when the target is a muxed VIDEO clip whose audio rides a sibling AUDIO clip (same asset + same timeline start), that sibling is replaced too (same new asset + source offset) so the A/V pair stays in sync; both halves are in-place equal-duration swaps so NEITHER track ripples (the linked-paste C-1 double-ripple trap cannot arise) and the two ops share one undo group. The core op allocates NO new clip id (the target keeps its id), so it is trivially replay-safe.

target_clip.description: Id of the clip whose slot to fill with the new source (project.state lists clips). Its timeline position + duration are preserved; its id is kept.

asset.description: Replacement source asset id (mutually exclusive with source_clip).

source_clip.description: Replacement source given as an existing clip id -- its asset + source window are used (mutually exclusive with asset).

source_in_ms.description: Source in-point (ms into the asset) the replacement starts from. Default 0 (or the source_clip's in).

source_out_ms.description: Caps the usable source (ms into the asset). Default = the source_clip's out, else the asset's probed duration.

link_audio.description: Also replace a muxed video clip's linked sibling audio (default true).

group_id.description: Optional undo-grouping tag for trusted orchestrators that replace this clip as part of a larger atomic edit.

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {target_clip, asset, track, slot_ms, new_src_ms, gap_ms, linked_audio?} -- the (kept) clip id, the new asset, its host track, the preserved slot duration, the realized source window, and gap_ms (>0 when the source was shorter than the slot and the remainder was padded). linked_audio is non-null when a muxed video clip's sibling audio was replaced too: {clip, track, new_src_ms, gap_ms}. One edit.replace op (two, grouped, when linked audio is replaced).

verbs.name: edit.fit_to_fill
verbs.description: FIT TO FILL: drop source footage into an EMPTY timeline slot and SPEED-ADJUST it so it exactly fills the slot. The fit speed = source_span / slot, so the retimed clip's timeline span lands back on the slot duration and NO downstream content moves (the gap is consumed in place, not rippled). The slot is [at_ms, at_ms+duration_ms) on `track`; when `duration_ms` is OMITTED it is inferred from the GAP currently at at_ms (fill THIS gap, from at_ms to the gap's end). The source is an imported `asset` or an existing `source_clip`; `source_in_ms`/`source_out_ms` window it (defaults: 0 / the source_clip's range / the asset's probed duration). Explicit source windows must stay inside the probed asset duration. The target span MUST be EMPTY -- a single gap that covers it, or the track tail -- fit_to_fill FILLS empty space, it does not overwrite media (delete the clip there first, which leaves a gap, or use edit.replace). The required speed must lie in the engine's retime range [0.25x, 4.0x]; if the source is too long or too short to fit, the verb errors with an actionable hint (trim the source / widen the slot). Single track, no linked audio (run it again on the audio track to speed-fit the matching audio slot). Lowers to ONE replay-safe edit.fit_to_fill core op (the resolved slot + source window + speed recorded so replay reproduces the fill; the placed clip's id pinned via added_clip).

track.description: Id of the track holding the slot/gap to fill.

at_ms.description: Timeline start of the slot to fill (ms).

duration_ms.description: Slot length (ms). Omit to fill the gap currently at at_ms (from at_ms to that gap's end).

asset.description: Source asset id (mutually exclusive with source_clip).

source_clip.description: Source given as an existing clip id -- its asset + source window are used (mutually exclusive with asset).

source_in_ms.description: Source in-point (ms into the asset). Default 0 (or the source_clip's in).

source_out_ms.description: Source out-point (ms into the asset). Default = the source_clip's out, else the asset's probed duration.

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {clip_id, track, at_ms, slot_ms, src_range_ms, speed, source_span_ms} -- the placed clip's id, its host track, the slot it fills, the source window used, the chosen fit speed (source_span/slot), and the source span. The clip occupies exactly slot_ms of timeline; downstream content is unchanged.

verbs.name: edit.split_edit
verbs.description: J-cut / L-cut (SPLIT EDIT): offset the AUDIO transition relative to the VIDEO cut at a clip boundary, so one clip's audio leads or lags its video -- the standard smooth-dialogue edit in every NLE. MODEL NOTE (see edit.detach_audio): a video clip's audio lives as a SEPARATE audio-track clip (the v1/a1t mirror), and clips trim/move independently. So a J/L cut is a ROLL of the AUDIO edit point against the (untouched) VIDEO cut, expressed as two ordinary edit.trims on the two linked AUDIO clips around the boundary. Because clip positions are CUMULATIVE, extending the outgoing clip's out-edge pushes the incoming clip's start later automatically and trimming the incoming clip's in-edge pulls its end back -- the net downstream effect is ZERO (a true roll), only the A|B audio boundary moves, the video is never touched. L-CUT (video leads, audio lags): extend A_audio out by offset_ms + trim B_audio in by offset_ms -> audio transition lands offset_ms AFTER the video cut (needs offset_ms of source past A_audio's out). J-CUT (audio leads, video lags): extend B_audio in EARLIER by offset_ms + trim A_audio out by offset_ms -> audio transition lands offset_ms BEFORE the video cut (needs offset_ms of source before B_audio's in). REQUIRES the audio to ALREADY be two clips butted at the cut (the natural distinct-sources state, each video clip with its a1t mirror). A single continuous audio clip across the cut has no audio transition to offset -> honest error pointing at edit.split / edit.detach_audio (the verb never silently splits the audio: that would allocate ids for zero semantic gain). v1 refuses a retimed (speed != 1) audio clip. Lowers to exactly TWO replay-safe edit.trim ops (no id allocation), grouped under one undo tag.

at_ms.description: The VIDEO cut position: the exact boundary (ms) between two adjacent video clips on the video track.
