kind.description: "l" = L-cut (video leads, audio lags: audio rolls AFTER the cut); "j" = J-cut (audio leads, video lags: audio rolls BEFORE the cut).

offset_ms.description: How far (ms) to roll the audio transition relative to the video cut.

video_track.description: Video track holding the cut. Omitted = the base (first) video track.

audio_track.description: Audio track holding the two linked clips. Omitted = the first audio track that holds both halves of the butted pair.

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {at_ms, kind, offset_ms, audio_a, audio_b, applied, audio_track, audio_boundary_ms, a_src_ms:{old,new}, b_src_ms:{old,new}} -- audio_a/audio_b are the two linked audio clips rolled; audio_boundary_ms is where the audio transition lands (at_ms +/- offset_ms); a_src_ms/b_src_ms are the before/after source windows (the only thing changed). Two grouped edit.trim ops appended.

verbs.name: edit.paste
verbs.description: Copy/Cut/Paste's PASTE half — duplicate a clip onto a track at a timeline position. THIN verb: it resolves a SOURCE clip to (asset, src_in, src_out) and LOWERS to edit.insert (the logged op is a self-contained edit.insert, so undo/diff/rebase already handle it — zero new core code). SOURCE: pass `clip` (the clip id to duplicate). SNAPSHOT FALLBACK: if `clip` is absent or no longer on the timeline, pass `asset` + `src_range_ms` so a clipboard snapshot whose source was deleted still pastes. `src_range_ms` (when `clip` is live) overrides the source window to paste a sub-range — REFUSED on a retimed (speed≠1) clip (the timeline→source mapping is non-linear there). KIND-CHECK (like edit.move): the source clip's track kind must match the destination track kind; caption clips are refused (use captions.*). RIPPLE: explicit `ripple` wins; omitted resolves from the destination track (base video/audio → true for AV sync, overlay/extra → false). LINKED AUDIO (`link_audio`, default true): when the source is a muxed VIDEO clip whose audio rides a sibling audio clip (same asset + same timeline start — the importer's linked-A/V signature), a SECOND edit.insert places that audio on its base audio track at the same at_ms (two ops, two undos). CURRENT LIMITS: insert-only (no overwrite), no effect/grade copy (a pristine duplicate), single source clip.

clip.description: Source clip id to duplicate. Optional: a snapshot paste of a since-deleted source uses asset + src_range_ms instead.

asset.description: Fallback source asset id, used when `clip` is absent or no longer on the timeline (requires src_range_ms too).

src_range_ms.description: Source sub-range [in,out] in ms. Omitted = the source clip's whole window. Refused on a retimed (speed≠1) source. REQUIRED for a snapshot (asset-only) paste.

ripple.description: Shift sibling tracks after at_ms by the pasted duration. Omitted = resolved from the destination track (base → true, overlay/extra → false), same rule as edit.insert.

link_audio.description: Also paste the source's linked sibling audio (a muxed video clip's audio on the base audio track) as a second insert at the same at_ms. false = the video clip only.

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {clip_id, ripple, rippled_tracks} — the pasted clip (the video insert's shape), its resolved ripple mode, and the rippled siblings; op_ids carries BOTH the video and (when link_audio resolved a sibling) the linked-audio insert

verbs.name: edit.gain
verbs.description: Set audio gain in dB on an AUDIO-track media clip OR an AUDIO track (exactly one of clip/track required). Video tracks contribute pixels only; imported video sound lives on its linked audio track, so video/caption targets are refused instead of storing a render no-op. Absolute set; the op records the old value.

clip.description: Media clip id on an audio track

track.description: Audio track id

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {target, kind: clip|track, old_db, new_db}; one op appended

verbs.name: edit.fade
verbs.description: Set LINEAR fades on a clip or a track. Clip form: provided fields are SET (in_ms = ramp from silence/black at the clip start, out_ms = ramp to it at the clip end; clip-local durations that travel with the clip through ripples), omitted fields keep their value, explicit 0 clears that side; 0/0 clears the fade. Track form: a convenience resolved NOW — in_ms lands on the track's FIRST media clip, out_ms on its LAST (the 'fade the music bed in/out' gesture); recorded as plain clip fades, so re-run it after restructuring the track (edit.duck doctrine). kind selects streams: audio = afade only, video = fade only, both (default) = whatever the track renders; a kind that cannot render on the target's track (audio on a video track — video tracks contribute no audio to the mix; video on an audio track) is refused, never a silent no-op. Render: video fades dip to/from BLACK on the base track and ramp ALPHA on overlay tracks (the overlay dissolves over the base); fades longer than the clip are clamped at render time. Splitting a faded clip leaves the fade-in on the left half and the fade-out on the right (a mid-clip split never invents a dip). HONEST SCOPE: linear ramps only, per-clip; CROSSFADES between adjacent clips are a v2 feature — adjacent fade-out + fade-in (a dip to black) is the v1 approximation.

clip.description: Target media clip id (exactly one of clip|track)

track.description: Target track id: in_ms → first media clip, out_ms → last media clip

in_ms.description: Fade-in length, ms (0 clears). At least one of in_ms|out_ms required; in+out must fit inside the clip

kind.description: Stream selector; one kind per clip fade (setting a fade replaces the kind)

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {targets: [{clip, track, old_fade, fade}]} — one entry per touched clip (track form may touch two); one op appended

verbs.name: edit.mute_range
verbs.description: NON-DESTRUCTIVE mute range on one media clip — the low-level half of mute-word (transcript.mute_words resolves word indices to these ranges). Adds one [start_ms, end_ms) range in SOURCE-ASSET time (the same clock as src_in/src_out) to the clip's mute_ranges list (normalized: sorted, overlaps/adjacency merged), surgically UNMUTES an interval with remove_ms (subtracts it from every stored range — overlaps shrink, strict supersets split, other mutes untouched), or clears the whole list with clear:true. SOURCE time is the point: the mute stays glued to the spoken content through trims/slips/splits with no op rewriting (fades/keyframes are clip-local; duck windows are timeline-time and go stale — this deliberately is neither). The renderer gates the clip's audio volume to 0 over each range's overlap with the visible source window, mapped to post-speed segment time (reverse is mirrored correctly). Refusals: the clip must be a MEDIA clip on an AUDIO track (muting a video-track clip would 'succeed' inaudibly — target the linked audio clip or edit.detach_audio first); the range must be non-empty and intersect the clip's current visible source window; speed-RAMPED clips are refused (a piecewise mapping would drift the gate off the word). Fully undoable (project.undo) and replay-safe.

clip.description: Media clip id on an AUDIO track.

range_ms.description: [start_ms, end_ms) to mute, in SOURCE-ASSET time (the src_in/src_out clock — NOT timeline ms). Exactly one of range_ms | clear.

remove_ms.description: [start_ms, end_ms) to UNMUTE, in SOURCE-ASSET time — subtracted from every stored range (surgical; other mutes untouched). Exactly one of range_ms | remove_ms | clear.

clear.description: true = remove ALL mute ranges from the clip (the unmute). Exactly one of range_ms | clear.

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: effect {clip, action: add|remove|clear, range_ms, mute_ranges: <the normalized resulting list>} — invalid_args when the target is not an audio-track media clip, the range is empty/non-intersecting, or the clip is speed-ramped

verbs.name: edit.transform
verbs.description: Set (or clear) geometry + opacity on a video clip. Normalized values are validated at the verb/core boundary: x/y = top-left corner as a fraction of frame width/height (0..1), scale = clip width as a fraction of frame width (0..1]; out-of-range values are rejected instead of clamped. Height scales proportionally (the clip is the full conformed frame, scaled). opacity = 0..1 alpha (1 = opaque). Identity (0,0,1,1) clears. LAYER CONTRACT: the first non-empty video track is the stable base canvas and every later video track composites above it in track order; empty tracks do not claim the base slot. Overlay transforms produce picture-in-picture over the lower composite. A base transform places/scales the picture over black, and base opacity (static or keyframed) blends against black. A hidden or gapped base remains black rather than promoting a higher layer. The same final transform/opacity stage applies after a base mask or power-window composite. The renderer only even-rounds/clamps already-valid pixel geometry to legal frame coordinates.

scale.description: Clip width as a fraction of frame width; 1 = full-frame

opacity.description: Clip alpha — 1 = fully opaque; overlays blend over lower layers, while the base blends against black; 0 = invisible

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {clip, transform, old_transform}; one op appended

verbs.name: edit.crop
verbs.description: Set (or clear) a video clip's SOURCE crop rectangle (framing correctness). Values are SOURCE PIXELS (x,y,w,h) — the rectangle of the source frame to KEEP, NOT normalized — because crop happens in source space BEFORE the conform/transform stages. COMPOSE ORDER (contract): crop -> conform (scale/pad to project geometry) -> overlay transform (PiP); the renderer inserts crop=w:h:x:y as the first filter after the source trim, so the project frame is then filled with the cropped picture. Canonical use: remove a baked-in letterbox/pillarbox reported as the import's content_bbox perception fact (e.g. an OBS canvas/window mismatch that bakes black bands into the source pixels). When the asset is probed the crop must lie fully inside the source geometry (x+w <= width, y+h <= height) — out-of-bounds is a hard error; an identity crop (origin + full source size) clears it (stored as no crop). Applies to media clips on video tracks only.

x.description: Left edge of the kept rectangle, source px

y.description: Top edge of the kept rectangle, source px

w.description: Width of the kept rectangle, source px

h.description: Height of the kept rectangle, source px

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {clip, crop, old_crop}; one op appended (crop is null when an identity crop cleared it)

verbs.name: edit.grade
verbs.description: Native color grade on a media clip (the 'hero look' pass). Two optional stages, applied in order at render: PARAMETRIC (ffmpeg eq) then a 3D LUT (lut3d). Parametric knobs: contrast (1=unchanged), brightness (0=unchanged), saturation (1=unchanged, 0=greyscale), gamma (1=unchanged), temperature_k (white balance in Kelvin, ~6500 neutral, lower=warmer; omit for none). lut is a path to a user.cube 3D LUT (e.g. an S-Log3->Rec.709 conversion), applied last — the path must exist and end in.cube (we ship NO LUT files to keep the artifact license-clean; pro LUTs are user-supplied). verbs.name: edit.add_mask
verbs.description: Add (or clear) a vector/freeform MASK on a BASE-track video clip — a region effect (blur/pixelate/black) scoped to a SHAPE, the region-blur / privacy-redaction primitive (region-scoped cleanup; blur a face/label; censor a password). shape: 'rect' (points = 2 opposite corners [[x0,y0],[x1,y1]]), 'ellipse' (points = [[cx,cy],[rx,ry]] centre + radii), or 'polygon'/freeform (points = the vertices, ≥3, drawn closed). All points are FRACTIONS of frame width/height (0..1). effect: 'blur' (default, gaussian; strength = sigma px, default 15), 'pixelate' (mosaic; strength = block px, default 16), or 'black' (solid censor). feather = soft-edge fraction of frame HEIGHT (0 = hard). invert = scope the effect OUTSIDE the shape. enabled:false (or omitting shape) CLEARS the mask. The renderer bakes a feathered shape alpha (resvg) and alphamerge+overlays the effect inside the region (CPU/software path); animatable later via keyframes/tracking. v1 renders on the BASE (first) video track only — an overlay-track clip is refused (clear error). A core op (replay-safe).

clip.description: Base-track video clip id.

shape.description: Region shape (polygon covers freeform). Required unless enabled:false.

points.description: Normalized points (fractions of frame W/H). rect/ellipse = 2 points; polygon ≥ 3.

feather.description: Soft-edge feather as a fraction of frame height (0 = hard edge; default 0).

invert.description: Scope the effect OUTSIDE the shape instead of inside (default false).

effect.description: What to do in the region (default blur).

strength.description: blur → gaussian sigma px (default 15); pixelate → block px (default 16); black ignores it.

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {clip, mask, old_mask}; one op appended

verbs.name: edit.redact
verbs.description: REDACTION — a TIME-BOUNDED privacy effect: blur / pixelate / black-box a SHAPE region on a BASE-track video clip, active ONLY during `range_ms` (clip-local [start,end] ms; omit = the whole clip). The editor-side complement to capture-time anonymization: redact a password / API key / face / PII that appears mid-edit in ANY footage (screen recordings, imported clips). Shares the mask field + render path with edit.add_mask but is SECURITY-FRAMED: `mode` is blur (default) / pixelate / box (solid black censor), and an unset blur/pixelate strength uses a heavier OVER-BLUR fail-safe (never under-redact). shape: 'rect' (points = [[x0,y0],[x1,y1]]), 'ellipse' ([[cx,cy],[rx,ry]]) or 'polygon' (vertices ≥3); all points are FRACTIONS of frame W/H (0..1). feather = soft-edge fraction of frame height; invert = redact OUTSIDE the shape. enabled:false (or omitting shape) CLEARS. Render: the baked shape alpha gates the effect (alphamerge+overlay) with `enable='between(t,…)'` for the range (CPU/software path). v1: BASE (first) video track only; one region per clip (multi-region + motion-tracked + OCR auto-detect are next). A core op (replay-safe). To make it FOLLOW a moving subject, track with edit.track then keyframe the region (until tracked-redact lands).

clip.description: Base-track video clip id.

shape.description: Region shape (polygon covers freeform). Required unless enabled:false.

points.description: Shape points as FRACTIONS of frame W/H: rect = 2 corners, ellipse = [centre, radii], polygon = vertices (≥3).

mode.description: Redaction effect: blur (default, gaussian) | pixelate (mosaic) | box (solid black censor).

feather.description: Soft-edge fraction of frame height (0 = hard edge).

invert.description: Redact OUTSIDE the shape instead of inside.

strength.description: blur → sigma px (fail-safe default 25); pixelate → block px (default 24); box → ignored.

range_ms.description: Clip-local [start_ms, end_ms] window the redaction is active in. Omit = the whole clip.

boxes.description: ADDITIONAL regions (face blur): blur/pixelate N faces or boxes at once, all sharing this `mode`/`strength`/`feather`/`range_ms`. Each box = {shape, points, track?} (fractions of frame W/H); track is the same [{t_ms,cx,cy}] motion-centre array as the primary region. The primary `shape`/`points` is region 0; `boxes` are the rest.

track.description: MOTION TRACK — the region CENTRE [{t_ms, cx, cy}] (fractions) over time, so the redaction FOLLOWS a moving subject. Feed edit.track's `points`. rect/ellipse shapes only; the shape gives SIZE, the track overrides the centre. The renderer animates the alpha procedurally (geq).

ocr_auto.description: OCR AUTO-DETECT — read the frame at `at_ms`, find on-screen PII (email/key/card/SSN/IP/JWT/AWS-key/secret-keyword) via OCR (RapidOCR) + regex, and redact the UNION region of all matches (fail-safe over-cover). Omits shape/points (computed). Needs the perception sidecar + rapidocr; returns found:0 (no op) when nothing sensitive is detected. The receipt reports CATEGORIES + box only, never the matched text.

faces.description: FACE AUTO-DETECT — detect every face in the frame at `at_ms` (YuNet, bundled) and BLUR them all at once (multi-region). The one-click privacy redaction for people's faces. Omits shape/points (computed → one box per face, margin-expanded). Shares this call's `mode`/`strength`/`feather`/`range_ms`. Needs the perception sidecar (opencv); returns found:0 (no op) when no face is detected at the frame.

track_faces.description: FACE AUTO-DETECT option: true/default tracks detected faces over time; false uses only the static detection frame. `track` remains the motion-track array for already-resolved redaction regions.

at_ms.description: Clip-local frame (ms) to scan for `ocr_auto` / `faces` (default 0). Pick the moment the secret / face is on screen.

pii.description: Restrict `ocr_auto` to these PII categories (default: all).

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {clip, mask, old_mask}; one op appended

verbs.name: edit.track
verbs.description: MOTION TRACKING — track a region across a clip's frames (cv2: CSRT, with a matchTemplate fallback) and return its trajectory plus ready-to-apply pos_x/pos_y (and optional scale) KEYFRAME arrays, so a title / PiP / blur-mask can FOLLOW the moving subject. Seed the tracker with `bbox` [x,y,w,h] OR a `point` [x,y] (all FRACTIONS of the frame, top-left origin). Tracks the clip-local window [start_ms,end_ms] (default the whole clip), sampling every `every_ms` (default 100). This is a MEASUREMENT (non-mutating, like verify.*): the op log stays cv2-free and replay-deterministic. BIND the result: feed keyframes.pos_x / keyframes.pos_y straight into edit.keyframe {param:'pos_x'|'pos_y'} on an overlay clip (position keyframes and masks consume these natively). Needs the perception sidecar (python + cv2); returns a setup hint if absent. Read-only.

clip.description: Media clip id to track in (its source pixels).

bbox.description: Seed box [x,y,w,h] as FRACTIONS of the frame (top-left origin). One of bbox/point is required.

point.description: Seed point [x,y] as fractions; a small box is grown around it. Alternative to bbox.

start_ms.description: Clip-local start of the tracked window (default 0).

end_ms.description: Clip-local end of the tracked window (default = clip duration).

every_ms.description: Sample interval in ms (default 100). The tracker updates every frame; this thins the emitted keyframes.

engine.description: Tracker engine (default auto → CSRT, else template fallback).

track_scale.description: Also emit a `scale` keyframe channel (box size relative to the first sample) for a zoom that follows the subject (default false).

verbs.result: {clip, engine, fps, source:{width,height}, window_ms, sampled, coverage, first, last, keyframes:{pos_x:[{t_ms,value}],pos_y,scale?}, points:[{t_ms,cx,cy,w,h,ok}], apply_hint}

verbs.name: edit.multicam_sync
verbs.description: MULTICAM AUDIO SYNC — align ≥2 clips of the SAME event (interview/podcast/concert shot on several cameras) by cross-correlating their AUDIO energy envelopes. Two cameras hear the same sound at the same wall-clock time, so the lag that best aligns their audio IS the time offset between the clips. Decodes each clip's audio to a 50 Hz RMS envelope, normalized-cross-correlates each against the `reference` (default the first clip) over ±`max_offset_ms` (default 15 s), and returns each clip's `offset_ms` + a confidence `score` (−1..1). MEASUREMENT (non-mutating, like edit.track): to SYNC, place/trim each clip by its offset (the agent applies it). Every clip needs an audio stream. Robust to per-camera gain (mean-subtracted + energy-normalized).

clips.description: ≥2 media clip ids of the same event.

reference.description: The clip all offsets are measured against (default: the first clip).

max_offset_ms.description: Max |offset| to search for (default 15000). Bounds the cross-correlation lag window.

verbs.result: {reference, env_hz, offsets:[{clip, offset_ms, score, reference?}], sync_hint} — offset_ms = how much LATER the clip's audio is than the reference

verbs.name: edit.multicam_switch
verbs.description: AUTO ACTIVE-SPEAKER multicam switching — given ≥2 audio-SYNCED camera angles of one scene (each on its own VIDEO track, already time-aligned on the timeline — run edit.multicam_sync and place the clips first), cut the program to whichever camera is the ACTIVE SPEAKER (loudest) over time: the interview / podcast multicam edit. Per 250 ms window across the angles' OVERLAPPING span, each camera's audio energy is read from its perception Loudness.windows envelope (the same audio facts edit.duck / edit.auto_zoom use), mapped to timeline coordinates; the loudest camera wins, with a small energy HYSTERESIS so two near-equal levels don't flicker. Adjacent same-camera windows merge into shots, and any shot shorter than `min_shot_ms` (default 1500) is dissolved, so there are no sub-second cuts. REPRESENTATION (replay-safe): an ORCHESTRATOR like assemble.broll — records NO op of its own; it wraps the build in an auto-checkpoint, (re)creates a reserved `__mc_program` VIDEO track ON TOP (later video tracks composite over earlier ones, so a full-frame opaque clip occludes the angles beneath → exactly one angle shows), and LOWERS each shot to a plain edit.insert of the active angle's segment at the sync-correct source offset. Existing user tracks named `program` are preserved and not auto-detected as camera angles. AUDIO is unchanged — video tracks contribute no audio to the render (it mixes from audio tracks only), so this switches the PICTURE, not the sound (standard multicam practice; no per-cut audio jumps). One dominant speaker → one shot / no switches (clean, not an error). <2 angles, an angle with no audio energy, or no overlapping span → an actionable error. SPEAKER-IDENTITY MODE (speaker-identity mode): when a diarization exists for the reference/`diarize_asset` (run media.diarize first), pass `mode:"speaker"` (or rely on AUTO) to cut to the camera of whoever is SPEAKING — each diarized speaker is mapped to the angle whose mic is loudest during their turns, so an off-camera loud noise no longer steals the shot; `mode:"energy"` forces the loudest-mic default. LIMITS: 250 ms window granularity; assumes the angles are already time-aligned; speaker→camera correlation needs per-angle mic separation.

tracks.description: The camera-angle VIDEO track ids to switch between (≥2). Omit to auto-detect every video track holding a media clip.

min_shot_ms.description: Minimum shot length, ms — no cut faster than this (the anti-flicker / no-sub-second-cut floor). Default 1500.

reference_track.description: The anchor / default angle the program opens on and falls back to on near-equal levels (must be one of `tracks`). Default: the first angle.

mode.description: SPEAKER-IDENTITY cutting (speaker-identity mode): "speaker" cuts to the camera of whoever is SPEAKING — each diarized speaker is mapped to the angle whose mic is loudest during that speaker's turns, so an off-camera loud noise no longer steals the shot (needs media.diarize on the reference/diarize asset). "energy" is the original loudest-mic behavior. Omit for AUTO: speaker mode when a diarization is available, else energy.

diarize_asset.description: The asset whose diarization (media.diarize speaker_turns) drives speaker mode. Default: the reference angle's asset. Must be one of the camera angles' assets (its track gives the timeline↔source mapping). Ignored in energy mode.

verbs.result: {shots:[{start_ms, end_ms, camera, energy}], switches, tracks, min_shot_ms, program_track, span_ms, mode, checkpoint, revert_hint, note} — the active angle of each shot is COMMITTED as a plain edit.insert onto the reserved `__mc_program` video track (an orchestrator: no op of its own; revert via the checkpoint; replay/diff need no diarization — diarization is read at PLAN time only). `camera` is the on-screen angle's track id, `energy` its mean momentary LUFS over the shot, `switches` = shots−1. `mode` reports {mode:"speaker"|"energy", and in speaker mode diarize_asset, num_speakers, speaker_to_cam:[{speaker, camera}]}

verbs.name: edit.eq
verbs.description: Parametric audio EQ on a clip — the audio analog of edit.grade, for cleaning up voice on talking-head / podcast / screen-demo audio. A high-pass (low-cut, removes rumble/HVAC), any number of peaking bands (presence boost, mud/de-ess cut), and a low-pass (high-cut, tames hiss). Two ways to specify: (1) a PRESET (the easy path) — voice (low-cut + de-mud + presence), warmth (low-mid body), de_rumble (subsonic cut), phone (telephone band-limit, a lo-fi effect), de_ess (tame sibilance), brighten (high-end air). (2) RAW high_pass_hz / low_pass_hz / bands[{freq_hz, gain_db, q}]. enabled:false (or an empty/identity EQ) CLEARS it. AUDIO-track media clips only (a video file's audio is a separate clip on its own audio track). Emitted as ffmpeg highpass → equalizer(per band) → lowpass on the clip audio; applies on both the software and GPU render paths (the GPU fast-track reuses the software audio chain).

clip.description: Media clip id (on an audio track)

preset.description: Named EQ shape; resolved to explicit high_pass/low_pass/bands

high_pass_hz.description: High-pass (low-cut) corner frequency, Hz (raw; omit for none)

low_pass_hz.description: Low-pass (high-cut) corner frequency, Hz (raw; omit for none)

bands.description: Peaking bands (raw; ignored when preset is given). A 0 dB band is dropped.

gain_db.description: Boost (+) or cut (-) at the centre, dB

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {clip, eq, old_eq}; one op appended

verbs.name: audio.cleanup_voice
verbs.description: One-shot talking-head / podcast VOICE CHAIN — the agent-first 'make my voice publish-ready' button. Applies a cleanup chain to the target audio clip(s): edit.eq{preset:voice} (low-cut rumble + de-mud + presence) THEN edit.effect{denoise, gate, compressor} (afftdn hiss/hum reduction -> agate room-tone-between-phrases -> acompressor dynamics + auto makeup gain). The render emits these in the fixed audio-chain order, so this is 'clean the voice', not surgical mastering. SCOPE: `clip` = one audio clip; `track` = every media clip on that audio track; neither = EVERY media clip on EVERY audio track (clean the whole project's voice in one call). `strength` (light|medium|strong, default medium) scales the denoise/gate/compressor amounts. ORCHESTRATOR: records no op of its own; wraps the sub-verbs in an auto-checkpoint and dispatches edit.eq + edit.effect as real replay-safe ops, so the whole pass reverts in ONE step (project.revert{to:checkpoint}) and replay needs no new arm. Stops on the first failing sub-verb and returns the checkpoint (never half-applied). Loudness is a RENDER-time setting (render.final{normalize_loudness}), not baked here — the receipt recommends a target in `loudness_hint`.

clip.description: Optional: clean ONLY this audio media clip (id from project.state). A video file's audio is a separate clip on its own audio track.

track.description: Optional: clean every media clip on THIS audio track (id from project.state). Must be an audio track.

strength.description: How hard to clean — scales the denoise/gate/compressor amounts. Default medium. The eq:voice tone shaping is fixed across strengths.

rationale.description: Optional human/agent rationale, recorded on every sub-op's receipt.

verbs.result: {status, strength, clips[], chain[], applied[], loudness_hint, checkpoint, diff, revert_hint}; orchestrator — appends an auto-checkpoint + edit.eq/edit.effect ops per clip, no op of its own

verbs.name: edit.slide
verbs.description: Animated-PiP convenience: slide an OVERLAY clip IN from / OUT to a screen edge over time — the easy path over hand-writing position keyframes. Reads the clip's resting transform (x/y/scale) + timeline length and LOWERS to an edit.keyframe op on pos_x or pos_y (so the op log records the resolved keyframes; replay never depends on this verb). edge: left/right → animates pos_x, top/bottom → pos_y. The off-screen position is the PiP's own size fraction off that edge; the resting position is the clip's static transform x/y (pair with a scaled edit.transform for the PiP size — an un-transformed full-frame overlay slides the whole frame). mode:'in' slides off-screen→rest over the first slide_ms; mode:'out' slides rest→off-screen over the LAST slide_ms. OVERLAY video media clips.

clip.description: Overlay media clip id

edge.description: Which screen edge to slide from/to (left/right → pos_x, top/bottom → pos_y)

mode.description: 'in' (off-screen → rest, at the clip start) or 'out' (rest → off-screen, at the clip end); default 'in'

slide_ms.description: Slide duration in ms (default 500; clamped to the clip length)

verbs.result: {clip, param, keyframes, old_keyframes}; one edit.keyframe op appended

verbs.name: edit.speed
verbs.description: Set (or clear) a media clip's playback SPEED factor (per-clip constant retime / slow-motion / speed-up). factor > 1 plays the clip faster, so it occupies LESS timeline (source_span / factor); factor < 1 is slow-motion (occupies more); factor 1.0 clears the retime back to normal. The clip's source range [src_in,src_out) is UNCHANGED — speed only remaps how that span lays onto the timeline (later clips ripple automatically) and time-stretches it at render (video setpts, audio atempo). A shortening retime is refused when an existing keyframe would fall beyond the new realized duration; move or clear that point first so animation is never silently unreachable. Pitch is PRESERVED by default so sped-up speech stays natural (not chipmunk); preserve_pitch:false (varispeed, pitch-follows-speed) is a reserved v2 effect and is rejected for now. Range 0.25–4.0. Media clips only (gaps/captions have no source to stretch).

clip.description: Clip id

factor.description: Speed multiplier: 2 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half speed (slow-mo), 1 = normal/clear

preserve_pitch.description: Keep pitch natural (default true). false (varispeed / pitch-follows-speed) is a reserved v2 effect, not yet supported.

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {clip, factor, old_factor, new_timeline_duration_ms}; one op appended

verbs.name: edit.speed_ramp
verbs.description: VARIABLE speed / time remapping — a clip whose playback speed CHANGES over its length (a speed curve or speed ramp, e.g. normal → fast → normal), vs the constant-speed edit.speed. `points` is a piecewise-LINEAR speed curve over the clip's SOURCE window: each {at_ms, factor} sets the playback speed `factor` at source offset `at_ms` (ms into the clip at natural 1× speed; 0 = clip start, src_out−src_in = its natural end); the speed interpolates linearly between points and holds the first/last factor outside their range. The clip is realized as `segments` contiguous CONSTANT-speed sub-segments sampled from the curve (the proven per-segment setpts/atempo path), so AUDIO is pitch-preserved (atempo per segment) and the realized timeline length = the integral of (1/speed) over the source = the sum of the sub-segment durations (later clips ripple automatically). New ramps retain the bounded `segments` request and bind it to the current project frame/sample grid; the current output grid may safely lower the effective filtergraph segment count, and a later project.format fps change restores the retained detail where permitted. Historic ramps recorded before this behavior retain their original millisecond replay. `segments` (default 24, clamped 2–120) trades smoothness vs filtergraph size — a ramp is a DISCRETE approximation of the curve, not a continuous warp. `points:[]` CLEARS the ramp (back to constant speed). preserve_pitch:false (varispeed) is a reserved v2 effect, rejected for now. Each factor must be in 0.25–4.0 (the validated retime range, matching edit.speed). The clip must be PLAIN: no constant speed≠1, reverse, freeze, animation, keyframes, matte, mask, or stabilize (those break the sub-segmentation — the verb refuses with a hint); time-invariant looks (gain/grade/effects/eq/crop) are fine. Media clips only. Splitting/trimming/sub-range-paste/detach are refused on a ramped clip (the timeline↔source map is non-linear) — clear the ramp first.

clip.description: Media clip id

points.description: Speed curve control points (≥ 2, strictly ascending by at_ms), OR [] to clear the ramp

at_ms.description: Source offset into the clip, ms (at natural 1× speed)

factor.description: Playback speed at this point: 2 = twice as fast, 0.5 = slow-mo

preserve_pitch.description: Keep pitch natural (default true). false (varispeed) is a reserved v2 effect, not yet supported.

segments.description: Number of constant-speed sub-segments the curve is sampled into (default 24). More = smoother ramp, larger filtergraph.

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: SET {clip, points, new_duration_ms, method, segments, preserve_pitch} (segments is the current grid-safe effective count) | CLEAR {clip, cleared:true, had_ramp, method}; one op appended

verbs.name: edit.crossfade
verbs.description: Crossfade (dissolve) the cut at at_ms on a track between two ADJACENT media clips. The cut at at_ms is the boundary between the clip ENDING there (LEFT) and the clip STARTING there (RIGHT); duration_ms is the overlap. duration_ms = 0 CLEARS an existing crossfade (back to a hard cut). The overlap is taken from the LEFT clip's tail + the RIGHT clip's head (each must carry at least duration_ms on its side), so the realized timeline SHORTENS by duration_ms across the crossfade (standard NLE centred-on-the-cut dissolve, like ffmpeg xfade len_a+len_b-D). Render: video uses xfade (transition=fade), audio uses acrossfade. Stored on the RIGHT clip so it travels with that clip through ripples (split keeps it on the LEFT half; a ripple_delete that removes the left neighbour clears the now-dangling crossfade). INTERACTION WITH edit.fade: a crossfade OWNS the cut, so setting one CLEARS the left clip's fade-OUT and the right clip's fade-IN (a per-clip fade there would double-dip); the clips' other ends keep their fades. Clearing the crossfade does NOT restore the cleared fades. Compose order is unchanged — crossfade is a seam operation between two already-conformed segments. Refuses caption tracks, gap neighbours, and positions that are not an exact clip-to-clip boundary (split first if needed).

at_ms.description: The cut point: a clip must END and another START exactly here

duration_ms.description: Dissolve length, ms; clamped to both neighbours' durations. 0 clears the crossfade at this cut.

transition.description: Transition STYLE for the VIDEO seam (audio is always a smooth crossfade). Omit / "fade" = classic dissolve. Others are ffmpeg xfade styles — call transitions.list for the full discovery catalog (name + family + direction + description). Families: dissolve (fade/fadeblack/fadewhite/fadegrays/fadefast/fadeslow/dissolve/distance/pixelize/hblur/radial), wipe (wipeleft/…/wipetl/…), slide (slideleft/…), smooth (smoothleft/…), cover (coverleft/…), reveal (revealleft/…), shape (circleopen/circleclose/circlecrop/rectcrop/horzopen/horzclose/vertopen/vertclose), slice (hlslice/…), diagonal (diagtl/…), squeeze (squeezeh/squeezev), zoom (zoomin), wind (hlwind/…). Ignored when duration_ms = 0.

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {at_ms, left_clip, right_clip, old_xfade_ms, xfade_ms, transition, fades_cleared} — fades_cleared lists any boundary fade the crossfade replaced; transition echoes the applied style; one op appended

verbs.name: edit.duck
verbs.description: Duck the music track under another track's speech: gain on music_track is reduced by `db` inside speech windows computed from against_track's perception silences (complement, mapped through the current EDL), with linear attack/release ramps. HONEST SEMANTICS: windowed gain computed NOW and recorded on the op — deterministic renders, exact db honored — NOT a render-time sidechain compressor; re-run after timeline changes that add/move speech (ripples DO remap existing windows). Replaces the track's previous duck windows. No speech found → no-op result, no op appended.

music_track.description: Audio track whose gain is reduced (the music bed)

against_track.description: Track whose speech drives the windows (needs perception reports on its assets)

attack_ms.description: Linear ramp length on each side of every window

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {track_id, windows_applied, replaced_windows, total_ducked_ms, windows} — one op appended (or {windows_applied: 0, note} with no op when the against-track has no speech)

verbs.description: Add a new empty video or audio track (compositing: music bed, overlay/PiP). project.create only makes v1/a1t. Ids are deterministic — video 'v{N}', audio 'a{N}t' — or pass an explicit unique id. Caption tracks are created by captions.* verbs instead.

verbs.name: edit.remove_track
verbs.description: Remove a track (closes the add-but-never-remove gap — an emptied overlay/music lane otherwise left a dead row with no way to clear it). Refuses the LAST video or LAST audio track (the renderer needs a base of each kind) and refuses a NON-EMPTY track unless `force` is set (so a stray click can't drop content). With force:true the track AND its clips go. Recompute-by-replay undo restores the track and its clips together. The UI auto-removes an emptied overlay track after a delete.

force.description: Remove the track even if it still has clips (drops them). Default false → a non-empty track is refused.

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {track_id, kind, clips_dropped}; one op appended (undo restores the track + clips)

verbs.name: edit.reorder_track
verbs.description: Move a track to a new STACKING position WITHIN ITS OWN KIND. Video track order is the compositing z-order — the first non-empty video track is the base canvas, each later video track overlays on top — so this brings a layer FORWARD (a higher same-kind index) or sends it BACK. `index` is group-relative: 0 means the first track of that kind, and it clamps to [0, same_kind_count-1]. A track can never cross into another kind group. Reordering audio/caption tracks is a render no-op (the renderer composites by kind) but allowed. Deterministic + replay-safe (records the resolved absolute from/to positions).

track.description: Track id to move (project.state lists ids)

index.description: Target position among tracks of the same kind (0 = first/bottom in that kind). Clamped to the last same-kind index.

verbs.name: audio.dub
verbs.description: Native AI DUBBING: re-voice an asset's speech into target_lang in a cloned `voice` (default "rebeka"), TIME-FIT to the original, and ADD it as a NEW audio track at the original segment timings. The ORIGINAL audio is KEPT (a mutable mix) — dubbing ADDS a track, it never replaces. Pipeline: read the asset's word-level transcript (it MUST be transcribed — media.transcribe first) → group into sentence-ish segments → TRANSLATE each segment into target_lang (REUSES the transcript.translate machinery: PRIMARY = the user's subscription CLI agent claude/codex/grok; FALLBACK = the local Opus-MT/MADLAD sidecar) → SYNTHESIZE each translated segment via the OmniVoice TTS service (dub_runner.py POSTs each with `duration` = the segment's [start,end] slot length, then `atempo`-trims the residual to hit the slot, and assembles ONE continuous 24 kHz mono WAV with each segment placed at its ORIGINAL start time, silence between) → IMPORT the WAV as an asset → place it as per-segment clips on a fresh `dub<N>` audio track (op-log, replay-safe; ripple:false so the dub floats and nothing shifts). The network touch (translate + synth) happens BEFORE the op is recorded, so a service failure fails the verb cleanly (never a fake/empty track) and replay/render stay OFFLINE. The TTS endpoint is CUT_DUB_ENDPOINT (default http://127.0.0.1:9001; set it before launch when the service uses a custom address). Voice-cloning a NEW speaker is an offline train job (out of scope here); this verb synthesizes with an EXISTING registered voice. Receipt (surfaced + written to receipts/<asset>.<lang>.dub.json): source_lang, target_lang, voice, model, n_segments, mean_fit_ratio, and per-segment {slot_ms, synth_ms, fit_ratio, placed_at_ms, placed_ms}.

verbs.name: captions.import

Commits as one edit._set_timeline op (replay/diff-clean). Requires an open project.

verbs.name: captions.translate
verbs.description: Translate the caption cues into target_lang (TEXT only -- no dubbing/audio/TTS), PRESERVING each cue's EXACT timeline range by default (one source cue -> one target cue at the SAME range_ms). BACKEND: PRIMARY = the user's OWN subscription CLI agent (claude/codex/grok -- the SAME CLI agent.chat uses; pure text in/out, NO MCP/tools), the best-quality path (idioms, names, gender, reading-time fit); FALLBACK = a LOCAL self-hosted model (Opus-MT light per-pair CC-BY, or MADLAD-400 universal via model) run by translate_runner.py in the perception venv (model DOWNLOADS on first use -- not bundled). backend:auto (default)=CLI if available else local; cli/local force one. mode:track (default) adds a NEW caption track in target_lang (source cues KEPT -> bilingual; the new track defaults to the TOP position so it doesn't collide with the bottom source cues). mode:replace overwrites the source cues' text in place (monolingual swap) only if cue ids/ranges/text still match the source read before translation; same-count concurrent cue edits return conflict instead of positional remapping. reflow:true is valid only with mode:track; it re-wraps/retimes the new translated track to reading-speed limits (a translation's length differs from the source) -- offered, not forced. Committed as ONE lowered edit._set_timeline step; the translated text is BAKED into the op so replay is deterministic (no CLI re-call). Source track = source_track, else cap1, else the first caption track.

source_lang.description: Source language. Optional for the CLI backend (the LLM auto-detects); REQUIRED for the local Opus-MT backend (per-pair).

mode.description: track (default) = add a target-language track (bilingual); replace = overwrite the source cues' text in place.

source_track.description: Caption track to translate. Default: cap1, else the first caption track (excluding the txt1 title-card track).

Separate from captions.generate's 'cap1' so regeneration never wipes text cards. HONEST SCOPE: styled static text — full motion-graphics titles (animation, per-word styling, fades) are a later feature. position without style_ref auto-creates a built-in title style txt_<position> (Inter 64, white on translucent black); neither → the Default bottom caption style. A card ending past the media end grows the composition (black behind the text) — warned in-band.

verbs.name: captions.kinetic
verbs.description: Animated, transcript-synced captions (the motion-graphics counterpart to captions.generate's STATIC burn-in): each caption LINE pops in (fade + scale-up) and fades out in sync with speech, rendered as a native title overlay (resvg per-frame; in-house, no external tool). Reads the EXISTING cap1 caption cues (run captions.generate first), optionally narrowed to range_ms (a cue is kept if it overlaps the range), builds a kinetic TitleSpec spanning [first cue start, last cue end], and places it on the TOP-MOST title1 overlay track — lowering to import + insert. Cue text + timing come straight from captions.generate (per-LINE animation; per-WORD sub-cue reveal is a follow-up). position = bottom (default) | center | top; color defaults white; font_px defaults to a fraction of the project height. Set replace_static:true to REMOVE the cap1 static cues this call animates (range-aware: cues outside an explicit range stay static) so the kinetic overlay shows ALONE; overlay placement and static-cue clear are grouped as one Undo action. Default false keeps the kinetic-over-static behavior. Generation cost scales with the span; narrow range_ms for long videos.

range_ms.description: Narrow to cues overlapping [start_ms, end_ms); omit for all cues

font_px.description: Font size in px at the project height (default ~5% of height)

replace_static.description: Remove the cap1 static cues this call animates so the kinetic overlay shows alone (range-aware). Default false.

per_word.description: PER-WORD ('karaoke') mode: animate each spoken WORD as its own centred cue (the 2026 word-by-word short-form style) instead of one cue per caption LINE. Reads word timings from the transcript via the EDL, so it does NOT require captions.generate first. Pairs with replace_static for a pure word-by-word look.
