verbs.name: render.reframe
verbs.description: Subject-aware auto-reframe (job, returns {reframe_id, job_id}). Renders the timeline to a temp at project geometry (the finished edit), runs the `subject` perception instrument (local CV: detect+track+saliency -> a normalized, aspect-independent subject track), then a subject-tracked moving-crop POST-PASS to the target aspect. The HONEST replacement for render.final{aspect,fit:cover} (which is a naive STATIC centre-crop that ignores the subject): this FOLLOWS the subject with a smoothed pan, original render untouched. Output default <project>/exports/<reframe_id>.mp4; an explicit fenced path must also end in .mp4. The receipt records subject-in-frame %, the device it analyzed on, and that reframe is a LOSSY crop (not a lossless conversion).

aspect.description: Target aspect ratio W:H with small integers, e.g. 9:16 (vertical), 1:1 (square), 4:5 (portrait), 16:9. Output dimensions are normalized to a 1080-px base, rounded even.

preset.description: Reframe preset: which subject classes to follow + the crop zoom/motion limits. talking_head (person, gentle), sports (person+vehicles, faster motion, less zoom), pets (dog/cat/person), cars (vehicles), general (all classes).

path.description: Optional explicit .mp4 output path (FENCED, canonicalized, no traversal/symlinks, project-or-outputs-dir only). Default <project>/exports/<reframe_id>.mp4.

direction.description: DIRECTOR brief from the foundation model: a per-scene framing decision that OVERRIDES the CV ranker for those scenes. Get the scenes + candidate subjects from render.direct's contact sheet, then map scene index -> the chosen candidate. Shape: {"<scene_idx>": {"cx": <0..1>}} to follow the subject at that normalized x (read each candidate's cx from the contact-sheet JSON), or {"<scene_idx>": {"mode": "widen"}} to hold a centered wide frame. Scenes you omit fall back to the CV ranker. The receipt records which scenes the director decided.

rationale.description: Optional human-readable reason for this reframe (recorded for the operation history; does not affect the output).

verbs.result: {reframe_id, job_id, aspect} — the output path + honesty receipt (subject_in_frame_pct, analyzed_on device, directed_scenes, reframe-is-lossy note) arrive in the job result; render_done event on completion

verbs.name: render.direct
verbs.description: DIRECTOR pass for subject-aware reframe (job): renders the finished edit to a temp and builds a SPARSE per-scene CONTACT SHEET — one annotated keyframe per scene with the candidate subjects labeled A/B/C left->right — for a foundation model to direct the whole clip in one look. The local CV finds and tracks subjects; the model decides which subject each shot is about. Flow: call render.direct -> read the returned contact_sheet image + scenes[].candidates -> decide per scene -> call render.reframe{aspect, direction:{<scene>:{cx}|{mode:'widen'}}}. Omitting the director falls back to the pure CV ranker.

preset.description: Which subject classes to consider as candidates (same set as render.reframe's preset). talking_head = person; sports = person+vehicles; pets = dog/cat/person; cars = vehicles; general = all.

rationale.description: Optional human-readable reason (recorded for the operation history; does not affect the output).

verbs.result: {job_id, direct_id} — the job result carries {contact_sheet (image path to read), scene_count, scenes:[{scene, t_ms, candidates:[{label, cls, cx, cy, box, has_face}]}]}; feed your per-scene pick into render.reframe{direction}

verbs.name: render.qc
verbs.description: DIRECTOR QC pass (job): REVIEW a reframed OUTPUT and decide what to fix. Resolves the actual render.reframe output from receipts/<reframe_id>.json output_path, with legacy fallback to exports/<reframe_id>.mp4. Samples one keyframe per scene of the finished reframe and tiles them into a review sheet WITH cheap CV composition hints per scene — subject_present, face_present, face centering (off_center = |cx-0.5|), headroom (face-top y; a head clipped at the top), and a `needs_review` flag. A foundation model reads the qc_sheet image and for any bad scene re-issue render.reframe{aspect, direction:{<scene>:{cx}|{mode:'widen'}}} with a correction. Closes the director loop: direct -> reframe -> qc -> reframe.

reframe_id.description: The reframe output to review — the reframe_id returned by render.reframe. The actual output is resolved from the reframe receipt output_path, with legacy fallback to exports/<reframe_id>.mp4. Fenced: a bare id, no path separators.

preset.description: Candidate class set for the QC detector (same set as render.reframe's preset).

rationale.description: Optional human-readable reason (recorded for the operation history; does not affect the output).

verbs.result: {job_id, reframe_id} — the job result carries {qc_sheet (image path to read), scene_count, review_count, scenes:[{scene, t_ms, subject_present, face_present, face_cx, off_center, headroom, needs_review, issues}]}; re-issue render.reframe{direction} to fix flagged scenes

verbs.name: render.final
verbs.description: Full deterministic render (job, returns {job_id}). Default path <project>/exports/<render_id>.mp4; an explicit FENCED path must match the chosen container: .mp4 for h264/hevc/av1, .webm for vp9, or .mov for prores. On completion AUTO-runs the output-only RenderChecks battery → RenderReceipt; receipt_ready is always emitted after render_done. The async job result reports verified plus verification_status complete|unmeasured. Optional post-render instrumentation failures preserve verification_error, mark affected receipt rows details.status=unmeasured/details.measured=false, and never create content fix_actions. Long or high-resolution timelines render in adaptive windows internally (segmented) so peak RSS stays bounded regardless of duration — output is byte-identical to a whole-graph render, so deterministic replay is preserved; on Linux each render also runs inside a transient cgroup memory soft-limit (throttle + spill, never a kill). Tune segmentation/footprint via the SHELLX_CUT_RENDER_* env knobs (see SKILL.md / reference.md Runtime knobs).

preset.description: Quality tier (geometry/fps come from project settings): draft = fast review encode (x264 medium CRF 18, AAC 192k), standard = default (x264 slow CRF 20, AAC 192k), high = hero-asset tier (x264 slow CRF 17, AAC 256k). The receipt records the preset used. Within a non-h264 `format` it shifts that codec's rate knob.

format.description: Output FILE FORMAT (codec + container) — 'different file exports'. h264 = universal mp4 + AAC, the default golden combo (byte-identical to omitting format). hevc = H.265 mp4 (Apple hvc1 tag), ~30-50% smaller at equal quality. vp9 = VP9 + Opus.webm, royalty-free web-native. prores = ProRes 422.mov, the pro editing-handoff intermediate. av1 = AV1 mp4, the highest quality ceiling but SOFTWARE-slow here (libsvtav1) — use hardware tier for AV1 speed. The output extension follows the container; `preset` selects the quality tier within the codec.

hardware.description: Encoder tier. auto (default) = use the GPU/hardware encoder when the machine has one (NVENC/QSV/AMF/VideoToolbox) — much faster, and hardware AV1 is the quality ceiling. off = force the software encoder (byte-deterministic, maximum libx264 quality, no GPU). Only h264/hevc/av1 have a hardware tier (vp9/prores are software-only). The hardware encoder is PROBE-VERIFIED with a real test encode, so auto safely falls back to software when no working GPU encoder is present. The receipt's preset field records the encoder that actually ran (e.g. 'standard/hevc_nvenc').

bitrate.description: Target VIDEO bitrate for rate-targeted publishing — e.g. '12M' (12 Mbps), '8000k', or a bare kbps number (50..500000 kbps). Omitted (DEFAULT) = quality-targeted CRF, byte-identical replay. Setting it switches the codec to a real bitrate target (needed to hit a platform spec — see export.publish). Works with the hardware tier (encoder-aware rewrite). ProRes ignores it (profile-fixed).

target_size_mb.description: Target output FILE SIZE in MB — 'fit under X' (Discord 25, email attach, WhatsApp). Computes the video bitrate that keeps the file UNDER the size (from the timeline duration, reserving audio, 90% headroom for VBR variance + container overhead) and renders VBR-under. Mutually exclusive with `bitrate`. Errors if the size is too small for the duration. ProRes ignores it.

rate_control.description: Rate control WHEN bitrate is set. vbr (default) = target AVERAGE, peaks capped ~1.45× for motion headroom; comes in UNDER on simple content (efficient — platform bitrates are ceilings). cbr = TRUE constant bitrate (x264 nal-hrd / x265 strict-cbr pad to the target) for strict-ingest platforms / live streaming. Errors if set without bitrate.

audio_bitrate.description: Target AUDIO bitrate — e.g. '384k' (YouTube), '192k' (social, the default). Omitted = the format's default (192k AAC). Lossless formats (wav, prores PCM) ignore it.

profile.description: Footage profile for the auto-run check battery (profile regression coverage): talking_head = the full strict battery; silent_screen_demo waives lufs/caption_presence/silence_at_edges (recorded as waived_by_profile with the measured outcome kept) and runs a UI-tuned frozen-frame check. NOTE: the uniform_border check `uniform_border` is NOT waived by any profile — a baked-in margin is a defect on screen demos too. The receipt's footage_profile entry records the active profile + auto-detect proposal.

fit.description: Framing fit for sources whose aspect differs from the output frame. contain (DEFAULT, unchanged behavior) = letterbox/pillarbox (scale to fit inside, pad black, no pixels lost). cover = crop-to-fill (scale to cover the frame, centre-crop the overflow). Independent of the quality preset. Omitting it replays byte-identical.

resolution.description: Output geometry. project (DEFAULT, unchanged behavior) = the project settings width×height. match_source = the largest source video geometry on the timeline (a cropped clip contributes its crop rect; fps/audio_rate still come from project settings) — keeps high-res footage at native resolution instead of conforming down. Omitting it replays byte-identical.

aspect.description: Reframe to this aspect for THIS render only (multi-format publish; project untouched): 9:16, 16:9, 1:1, 4:5, etc. Maps to 1080-baseline dims; defaults fit to cover. Mutually exclusive with resolution and width/height.

width.description: Explicit output width px (with height; 16..=7680). Overrides resolution; defaults fit to cover. Mutually exclusive with aspect/resolution.

normalize_loudness.description: Optional target integrated loudness in LUFS. Omitted = no normalization (byte-identical replay). When set, single-pass ffmpeg loudnorm brings the mixed audio to this target (TP -1 dBTP, LRA 11) — closes the measure(lufs check)->target loop. Standard targets: -16 (long-form), -14 (social), -23 (EBU R128).

dry_run.description: When true, return the render PLAN (output geometry, realized duration, per-track manifest, the checks that will run) WITHOUT encoding — verify before a slow render. No job/op/file.

verbs.result: {job_id, render_id} — receipt arrives via receipt_ready / verify.checks

result_schema.x-async-result: shellx-cut://receipts.schema.json#/$defs/RenderReceipt (arrives via receipt_ready / verify.checks; carries checks[] + fix_actions[] for the autopilot self-fix loop)

verbs.name: verify.checks
verbs.description: Run (or fetch) the deterministic check battery for a render: cut_on_word, lufs, caption_presence, black_or_frozen_frames, uniform_border (fails on a baked-in letterbox/pillarbox; NOT waived by any footage profile), silence_at_edges, duration_matches_edl. Each → {name, pass, details, evidence}.
verbs.result: RenderReceipt {render_id, checks: CheckResult[], pass, output_hash, …}

verbs.name: verify.rerun
verbs.description: Re-run output-only checks against the exact existing render artifact named by render_id. This job fences the receipt output, verifies its full SHA-256 before the sidecar, before ffprobe, and before its separate result receipt, and shares one cancellation/deadline/process-tree owner across the sidecar and ffprobe. It never re-encodes, changes the timeline, or overwrites the source RenderReceipt. The result includes lufs, black_or_frozen_frames, uniform_border, silence_at_edges, and duration_matches_receipt only; timeline/source checks remain on the original receipt.

render_id.description: Persisted render receipt id whose authorized output will be checked again.

verbs.result: OutputCheckRerunHandle {job_id, render_id, output_hash}; jobs.status.result becomes the separately persisted OutputCheckRerun {source_receipt_id, verification_receipt, scope:'rendered_output', profile, checks, pass, checked_at}. The source render receipt is immutable.

verbs.name: verify.pacing
verbs.description: On-demand pacing report for the CURRENT timeline (in-editor retention/pacing critique). Pure structural analysis of the base video track's shots — no render, no model. Advisory, not pass/fail.
verbs.result: {duration_ms, shot_count, internal_cuts, cuts_per_min, mean_shot_ms, median_shot_ms, shortest_shot_ms, longest_shot_ms}

verbs.name: verify.captions
verbs.description: Caption-QC receipt : measures each caption cue against the published timed-text standards — reading speed (chars/sec), on-screen duration, inter-cue gap, line length. Thresholds default to BBC/Netflix values (17 CPS, 833ms min / 7s max display, 80ms min gap, 84-char line cap) and are overridable per call. Read-only measurement; pass=true only when every cue is within spec.

min_gap_ms.description: Min gap between consecutive cues; smaller nonzero gaps flag as flicker (default 80).

max_chars.description: Max characters per cue (2 lines x 42 = 84 default).

verbs.result: {cue_count, pass, max_cps, mean_cps, violations:{too_fast,too_short,too_long,too_long_text,short_gap,overlap}, thresholds}

verbs.name: verify.delivery
verbs.description: Verbal-pacing receipt (complements verify.pacing's visual pacing): speaking rate (WPM, speech + articulation), filler density, and longest unbroken stretch, measured over the SOURCE transcript(s). Thresholds default to published speaking-rate guidance (flag <100 or >170 WPM, >3 fillers/min) and are overridable. asset narrows to one asset; omitted aggregates every asset with a transcript. Read-only; scope:source (raw recording, pre-cut).

asset.description: Measure only this asset (default: all assets with a transcript).

lexicon.description: Filler words to count (default um/uh/erm/ah/hmm/mhm — same lexicon as transcript.remove_fillers).

pause_gap_ms.description: Inter-word gap above which speech is 'broken' for the longest-unbroken-stretch measure (default 600).

verbs.result: {scope, word_count, speaking_ms, wpm, articulation_wpm, filler_count, fillers_per_min, filler_pct, longest_unbroken_ms, pass, flags:{too_fast,too_slow,high_fillers}, thresholds}

verbs.name: verify.loudness
verbs.description: Integrated-loudness RECEIPT for one audio-bearing asset: integrated loudness (LUFS), true peak (dBTP), loudness range (LRA), gating threshold, the gap to a target, and a one-line recommendation. The MEASURE half of the loudness loop — the NORMALIZE half is render.final's `normalize_loudness` (a rendered output's loudness is already checked by verify.checks/render.qc). Single fast ffmpeg `loudnorm` analysis pass (no re-encode); ffmpeg-only, needs NO perception venv. Read-only. Standard targets: -14 social, -16 long-form/podcast, -23 EBU R128. Use it to decide whether (and how far) to normalize before publishing, then re-check the render with verify.checks.

asset.description: The audio-bearing asset id to measure (a source clip, imported music, or a re-imported render).

target_lufs.description: Target integrated loudness to compare against (default -14, social). gap_lu = measured - target; within_tolerance = |gap| <= 1 LU.

verbs.result: {asset, integrated_lufs, true_peak_dbtp, lra, threshold_lufs, target_lufs, gap_lu, within_tolerance, true_peak_ok, recommendation, reference_targets:{social,podcast,ebu_r128}}

verbs.name: verify.scopes
verbs.description: VIDEO-SCOPES evidence for ONE frame — objective signal data measured with ffmpeg signalstats, so the agent reads NUMBERS instead of guessing colour from a thumbnail (the verify.* philosophy applied to the picture; complements render.qc). Reports luma min/avg/max, highlight/shadow CLIPPING, BROADCAST-range legality (Rec.709 limited [16,235]), saturation avg/max, white-balance CAST (from the Cb/Cr means), and hue. Source: the COMPOSED timeline frame at at_ms (default 0), or a source `asset`'s frame at at_ms. The analysis never changes project history, but it materializes a fenced exports/scopes/frame_<at_ms>ms.jpg; scope_images:true ALSO writes the classic scope PNGs (vectorscope/waveform/histogram — `kinds` filters which) for a human/VLM to eyeball. The receipt's `flags` (clipped_highlights/crushed_shadows/illegal_levels/colour_cast/over_saturated) + `pass` drive a grade fix (edit.grade). ffmpeg-only, no perception venv.

at_ms.description: Frame position (composition-local ms; default 0). For an asset, the seek offset into that source.

asset.description: Measure a SOURCE asset's frame at at_ms instead of the composed timeline frame.

scope_images.description: Also render the scope PNGs (vectorscope/waveform/histogram) under exports/scopes/ (default false — stats only).

kinds.description: Which scope images to render when scope_images:true (default all three).

verbs.result: {at_ms, source, frame, luma:{min,avg,max}, clipping:{highlights,shadows}, broadcast_legal, saturation:{avg,max}, white_balance:{u_avg,v_avg,cast}, hue:{avg,med}, flags:[...], pass, scopes?:{vectorscope,waveform,histogram}}

verbs.name: verify.brand
verbs.description: Brand-constraint receipt: prove the project's stored caption styles + output geometry conform to brand constraints. With no args, uses the durable project.brand kit; explicit fields form a validated one-call override. Checks font allow-list, colour palette (text+bg), caption position, font-size bounds, and output aspect. Read-only; pass=true only when every pinned constraint is satisfied.

colors.description: Allowed colours for caption text+bg, hex (#rgb/#rgba/#rrggbb/#rrggbbaa).

aspect.description: Required output aspect as W:H (e.g. 16:9); compared reduced against project geometry.

verbs.result: {source: stored|explicit, styles_checked, pass, note?, violations:{font,color,position,size,aspect}, brand}

verbs.name: verify.judge
verbs.description: Perceptual review of a render as a background job (returns {job_id, render_id}; a review takes ~0.5-3 min depending on rung). JUDGE ACCESS LADDER: spawns the judge ladder, which drives the user's OWN coding-agent CLI as a subprocess vision judge (frames + instrument facts + op-derived edit intent in, post-filtered structured verdict out; vision-only: listened=false, measurement-class claims stripped — instruments own all measured verdicts). The ladder auto-detects available CLIs in order claude -> codex -> antigravity -> grok (the shellX provider set; first found wins), or `backend` forces a specific rung. When NONE is available the job still COMPLETES with an honest SKIP (status not_run + skip_verdict "skipped" + a reason on the receipt naming each absent rung — visible, never silent, never a fake pass). The judge-review envelope (schema shellx-cut/judge-review/1) is attached at RenderReceipt.judge, the receipt re-persisted, and receipt_ready RE-EMITTED. Honest statuses: completed | not_run (no judge available, or an explicitly-forced rung's CLI is absent — NEVER a fake pass; job completes) | error (a rung attempted and failed — envelope attached, job fails with the cause).

render_id.description: Default: the most recent render receipt

backend.description: Which rung of the judge access ladder to run. "auto" (default; "cli" is a backward-compatible alias) walks the ladder claude -> codex -> antigravity -> grok and runs the first detected subscription CLI; "claude"/"codex"/"antigravity"/"grok" force that rung (honest not_run if its CLI is absent — an explicit override never silently falls through to a different provider). All four supported rungs are vision judges: claude, codex, antigravity (Google `agy`, the Gemini CLI successor), and grok (Grok Build CLI with native vision through ACP image blocks). Unknown ids fail fast.

verbs.result: {job_id, render_id} — job result: {render_id, status: completed|not_run|error, verdict?, confidence?, issues?, outcome?, outcome_reason?, reason?, receipt}; verdict is the model's raw word (pass|fail|needs_review) and `outcome` is the NORMALIZED gate decision derived from it (approve|reject|advisory — pass→approve, fail→reject, else→advisory; not_run→advisory) so a gate/autopilot can act on a rejection without parsing each CLI's vocabulary. The full envelope lands at RenderReceipt.judge (verdict at judge.review.verdict; a no-judge SKIP shows status=not_run + judge.skip_verdict="skipped" + judge.ladder.skipped=true); receipt_ready re-emitted with the updated receipt

verbs.name: verify.pregate
verbs.description: PRE-RENDER PREDICTIVE QUALITY GATE (a 'pre-render gate + refuse-to-present', made rigorous on our op-log). Reasons over the OPEN project's CURRENT EDL + whatever per-asset perception reports are ALREADY CACHED — NO render spent, no model — and PREDICTS the render problems with a known structural signature so the agent can refuse to 'present' a likely-broken render BEFORE paying for it. Risk kinds: empty_tail (HIGH — the timeline runs past the last VIDEO clip ⇒ plays into BLACK; a real shipped-bug class), black_or_frozen (HIGH — a clip's source overlaps a detected black/frozen span ⇒ dead footage in the cut), slideshow_risk (MED — too few cuts over a long timeline ⇒ the 'slideshow'), silent_output (MED — no audio-bearing clip, or audio that is mostly silence per facts), tiny_or_zero_clips (MED — a media clip shorter than one frame never renders a visible frame), uniform_border (LOW — a clip's asset carries a baked-in letterbox/pillarbox). pass=false IFF any HIGH risk. HONEST: these are PREDICTIONS over structure + cached facts, NOT guarantees — a clean pregate means 'no KNOWN structural problem' (it can't see what the facts don't carry), and a flagged risk is a strong predictor not a certainty (an INTENTIONAL black outro trips empty_tail; a single long take trips slideshow_risk). Missing perception is never an error: assets with no cached report are skipped and listed in uninstrumented_assets (a clean pass over un-analyzed footage is weaker — and visibly so). Read-only: no op, no render, no model.
verbs.result: {pass, risks:[{kind, severity:high|med|low, detail, range_ms?}], summary, thresholds:{empty_tail_tolerance_ms, black_frozen_min_ms, slideshow_min_duration_ms, slideshow_min_cpm, silent_fraction, frame_ms}, perception_assets, uninstrumented_assets:[...]} — pass=false iff a HIGH risk stands; risks carry the numbers behind each verdict and a timeline range_ms when one applies

verbs.name: export.frame
verbs.description: Extract a STILL FRAME: render the composed frame at at_ms at FULL project resolution and save it to the default export folder as frame_<ms>.jpg. By default (to_asset) ALSO imports the saved image as a new asset, so the frame shows in the Assets tray (draggable / insertable) AND is a real file on disk importable into another project. NON-DESTRUCTIVE — nothing on the timeline changes. The agent/UI passes at_ms (e.g. the playhead).

at_ms.description: Timeline position (ms) of the frame to extract

to_asset.description: Also register the saved frame as a new image asset (default true). false = just write the file.

path.description: Optional explicit .jpg or .jpeg output path for the still frame (FENCED). Default: the session output dir (project.set_output_dir) or <project>/exports/frame_<ms>.jpg.

verbs.result: {path, asset_id?, job_id?} — the saved JPG; asset_id/job_id present when to_asset

verbs.name: export.range
verbs.description: Save a PART OF THE TIMELINE as a reusable clip: render the composed timeline over [range_ms[0], range_ms[1]) (all effects baked) to exports/range_<in>_<out>.mp4 and, by default (to_asset), import it as a NEW asset. The saved clip lands in the Assets tray (draggable / insertable) AND on disk (importable into another project). NON-DESTRUCTIVE — the timeline is unchanged. The UI passes the selected clip's span (or in/out points).

range_ms.description: [start_ms, end_ms) timeline window to save (end > start)

to_asset.description: Also register the saved clip as a new asset (default true). false = just write the file.

path.description: Explicit .mp4 output file path (fenced). Default: the session output dir (project.set_output_dir) or <project>/exports/range_<in>_<out>.mp4.

verbs.result: {path, asset_id?, job_id?} — the saved mp4; asset_id/job_id present when to_asset

verbs.name: export.audio
verbs.description: Export the timeline's MIXED AUDIO as an audio-only file. Renders the same audio graph as render.final (per-track mix with gains/fades/speed) WITHOUT video, into <project>/exports/audio.<ext> (downloadable via /api/export). Synchronous like the other export.* verbs. format: mp3 (lossy, universal) | m4a/aac (lossy, Apple) | wav (uncompressed PCM) | flac (lossless) | opus (modern lossy, best at low bitrate); default mp3. An explicit FENCED path must use the selected container suffix (aac uses .m4a).

format.description: Audio file format. mp3 = universal lossy (default), m4a/aac = Apple lossy, wav = uncompressed PCM, flac = lossless compressed, opus = modern lossy (best quality per bit).

path.description: Optional explicit output path with the selected format suffix (FENCED; aac uses .m4a). Default exports/audio.<ext> (or exports/audio_<track>.<ext> for a per-track stem).

track.description: Optional: export ONLY this audio track's contribution (its processed audio incl. gain + ducking, at full timeline length) = a per-track STEM. The sum of every track's stem == the full mix (WYSIWYG). Powers the mixer's per-track meters. ids from project.state (audio tracks only).

to_asset.description: Also import the exported audio as a project asset (Assets tray — reusable as a music bed etc.). Adds {asset_id, job_id} to the result. Default false = just write the file.

verbs.result: {path, format, duration_ms, hash, track} (+ {asset_id, job_id} when to_asset) — the exported audio file (in exports/, downloadable via /api/export); track echoes the stem id (null for the full mix)

verbs.name: export.publish
verbs.description: ONE-CLICK platform export. Resolves a platform id to its 2026-researched encoding spec (output geometry, video + audio bitrate, H.264/mp4) and delegates to render.final with those args — reusing the full render path (background job, auto-run check battery, receipt). The optional `profile` passes through verbatim to render.final's footage-profile check battery (omit = render.final's default). Vertical platforms (tiktok/reels) output 9:16 via explicit geometry + cover fit; YouTube/X output 16:9. The result carries the chosen platform spec under `publish`, plus render.final's {job_id, render_id}. This is convenience over render.final — an agent can equally call render.final{width,height,bitrate,format,...} directly. fps comes from the project settings (a publish does not resample fps). For SUBJECT-AWARE vertical reframing use render.reframe instead.

platform.description: Target platform. youtube = 1920×1080 12 Mbps AAC 384k (16:9). youtube_4k = 3840×2160 45 Mbps. tiktok = 1080×1920 12 Mbps (9:16, alias shorts). reels = 1080×1920 10 Mbps (9:16, alias instagram/ig). instagram_feed = 1080×1350 10 Mbps (4:5). x = 1920×1080 20 Mbps (16:9, alias twitter). square = 1080×1080 10 Mbps (1:1). All H.264/AAC/mp4 — the universal ingest combo.

preset.description: Quality tier passthrough to render.final (encoder effort); the bitrate target is fixed by the platform spec.

hardware.description: Encoder tier passthrough. auto = use the GPU encoder when present (faster); off = software (deterministic).

profile.description: Footage profile passthrough to render.final's auto-run check battery: talking_head = the full strict battery; silent_screen_demo waives lufs/caption_presence/silence_at_edges (recorded as waived_by_profile with the measured outcome kept) and runs a UI-tuned frozen-frame check. Omit for render.final's default behavior (strict battery + auto-detect proposal in the receipt) — a silent screen demo published without this gets caption/loudness FAILs on the receipt that are profile noise, not defects.

path.description: Optional explicit .mp4 output path (FENCED). Default exports/<render_id>.mp4.

dry_run.description: Return the render PLAN (geometry, duration, checks) WITHOUT encoding — verify the platform target before a slow render.

verbs.result: {job_id, render_id, publish:{platform, label, width, height, video_bitrate, audio_bitrate, rate_control, format}} — receipt arrives via receipt_ready / verify.checks

verbs.name: export.gif
verbs.description: Export a SHORT timeline window as a looping animated GIF (the social/reaction-clip export). Renders the window (all effects baked, like export.range) then converts via the high-quality ffmpeg palettegen/paletteuse path (per-clip optimised 256-colour palette + dithering — far better than a naive GIF). Default range = the first 15s; HARD-CAPPED at 30s (GIFs balloon). fps (default 12) and width (default 480px, height auto) are the file-size levers. Output exports/gif_<in>_<out>.gif (FENCED); imports as an asset by default (to_asset).

range_ms.description: [start, end) timeline window in ms. Default = [0, min(duration, 15000)]. end-start must be ≤ 30000 (GIF cap).

fps.description: Frame rate (clamped 2..50). 10-15 = good motion/size balance; lower = smaller file.

width.description: Output width px (clamped 64..1920); height auto-derived even, lanczos downscale. Smaller = smaller file.

dither.description: Palette dithering. floyd (default) = error diffusion, smoothest gradients; bayer = ordered texture, smaller; none = hard quantize, smallest but bands.

to_asset.description: Also import the GIF as a project asset (Assets tray). false = just write the file.

path.description: Explicit .gif output file path (fenced). Default: the session output dir (project.set_output_dir) or <project>/exports/gif_<in>_<out>.gif.

verbs.result: {path, fps, width, range_ms, asset_id?, job_id?} — the GIF in exports/ (downloadable via /api/export)

verbs.name: export.xml
verbs.description: Export the timeline as NLE interchange XML (fcpxml / premiere / resolve). Default path <project>/exports/timeline.<ext>; an explicit FENCED path must use .fcpxml for fcpxml/resolve or .xml for premiere.
verbs.result: {path, format}

verbs.name: export.otio
verbs.description: Export the timeline as OpenTimelineIO (.otio) JSON — the industry-standard interchange (ASWF, Apache-2.0) that round-trips with DaVinci Resolve / Premiere / Final Cut, richer than the XML formats. Maps each video/audio track + clip to OTIO Track/Clip with source_range (RationalTime frames) + ExternalReference media; gaps → Gap. Times use the project fps. Caption tracks are not representable in OTIO and are omitted (warned in-band; use export.srt/vtt/ass). Default path <project>/exports/timeline.otio; an explicit FENCED path must end in .otio. The .otio is byte-lossless for Cut's timeline (the model round-trips export→parse).
verbs.result: {path, format:"otio"} — warns `captions_not_in_otio` when caption tracks are present

verbs.name: export.edl
verbs.description: Export the timeline as a CMX3600 EDL (.edl) — the universal edit-decision-list interchange every NLE and color suite reads (DaVinci Resolve / Premiere / Avid / Final Cut). Built from the same frame-quantized timeline as export.xml/otio, so the cut points line up to the frame. One numbered event per clip: channel V for the video track, A/A2/A3... per audio track; source reel = the file stem sanitised to <=8 uppercase alphanumerics, with a `* FROM CLIP NAME:` comment carrying the real filename for relink. NON-DROP FRAME timecodes against the rounded fps; EDL out-points are EXCLUSIVE. Gaps are implicit (the next event's record-in jumps forward). EDL is a CUTS-ONLY format: transitions, effects, grades, per-clip gain, speed changes and captions cannot be represented and are dropped (a `richness_dropped` warning lists what was omitted). Default path <project>/exports/timeline.edl; an explicit FENCED path must end in .edl. `title` names the sequence (defaults to the project name).
verbs.result: {path, event_count} — warns `richness_dropped` (with a `dropped` list) when the project carries transitions/effects/grades/gain/speed/captions the EDL cannot represent

verbs.name: import.otio
verbs.description: Preview or atomically import a foreign OpenTimelineIO (.otio) timeline. `mode:"preview"` performs a bounded (16 MiB), read-only structure/count/media-availability pass and returns a SHA-256 `source_hash`; `mode:"replace"` (default) optionally requires that hash, probes every available referenced media file before mutation, then adds new assets and replaces the active timeline in ONE replay-safe, undoable `import.otio` op. Missing media clips are preserved as timed gaps with an `otio_media_missing` warning. Unsupported nested stacks/transitions/effects/markers, disabled or cropped items, generated media references, invalid time values, wrong media kinds, source ranges beyond media duration, remote file authorities, and non-file URI schemes are refused rather than silently dropped. The current project format is preserved; source geometry is reported for an explicit later project.format decision. Caption tracks are not in OTIO.

mode.description: preview is read-only; replace is the default atomic timeline import

expected_hash.description: Optional source_hash returned by preview; replace conflicts if file bytes changed

verbs.result: preview -> {status:"preview", source_hash, tracks, track_count, clips, gaps, media_available, media_missing, missing_sources, source_format, format_policy:"preserve_project"}; replace -> {status:"imported", source_hash, tracks_created, clips_inserted, gaps, missing_clips, assets_imported, assets_reused, jobs, source_format, format_policy:"preserve_project"} with one op id; warns `otio_media_missing` when missing clips became timed gaps

verbs.name: export.srt
verbs.description: Export captions as .srt — the ONLY SRT exporter (captions.export_srt dropped). Default path <project>/exports/captions.srt; an explicit FENCED path must end in .srt.
verbs.result: {path, caption_count}

verbs.name: export.vtt
verbs.description: Export the caption track to WebVTT (HTML5 <track> standard for web-published video). Default <project>/exports/captions.vtt; an explicit FENCED path must end in .vtt.

path.description: Output .vtt path (default exports/captions.vtt).

verbs.name: screen_record.doctor
verbs.description: Report the SCREEN RECORDER's capability cards (the recorder analog of system.doctor). IN-PROCESS: probes record_capture::doctor() directly — no sidecar binary, no spawn — and returns each capability as a card {name, status, detail}. A screen_capture `ok` means one bounded, discarded frame reached Cut; `unknown` means a backend was found but a non-disruptive proof would require an OS picker, permission prompt, or live stream, and is never ready. `degraded`/`missing` are evidenced failures. The probe stores no image or audio content and stops before returning. `ready` requires ffmpeg, screen_capture, and input_hook, plus platform-required cards when present (Linux gstreamer/pipewiresrc and the session input path). The separate optional `system_audio` card is deliberately `unknown` when its platform backend is compiled: Doctor never opens a loopback/tap stream, and on macOS therefore never triggers the separate Audio Capture prompt. This optional card does not gate ordinary screen recording. `start_allowed` is deliberately narrower: it is true only when `screen_record.start` may proceed; on Linux that includes the exact prompt-deferred XDG ScreenCast portal observation so the user-initiated action can show its source picker, while Doctor stays unknown/non-green. Any missing, degraded, or other unknown required card keeps it false. Camera capture is reported unavailable until a real backend is implemented and does not gate screen recording. Also returns `monitors` (the displays for the in-app picker; empty on Linux/headless), `windows` (the app windows for the in-app WINDOW picker — record one app, not the whole screen; Windows-only), and, when `warm_mic:true`, `mic_warm` (the microphone pre-warm). No project required. A build/OS with no live-capture backend reports honestly, never panics.

The optional system_audio card stays unknown for a compiled backend until an actual recording proves packets and does not gate ordinary screen recording. ready iff the core capture cards and any platform-required cards are ok. start_allowed is the action-specific screen_record.start admission: it is false for missing, degraded, or arbitrary unknown required cards, and true on Linux only for the exact prompt-deferred XDG ScreenCast portal card so the user may choose a source. monitors + windows are empty on Linux/headless (the OS portal owns source choice) and populated on Windows (windows feeds the in-app app-window picker for screen_record.start{window}); mic_warm present only when warm_mic:true. not_found if no capture backend is compiled for this build/OS.

verbs.name: screen_record.system_audio_probe
verbs.description: Run one explicit, bounded native system-audio delivery and signal test without starting screen capture or creating a project. This is the consenting counterpart to passive screen_record.doctor: it opens the platform loopback/process-tap path for 0.5–5 seconds, so macOS may show the separate Audio Capture permission prompt. The caller should play a sound during the window. Captured samples are held only long enough to distinguish packet delivery from an all-silent route; Linux/Windows use an exclusively-created private temporary WAV that is removed before return, macOS keeps samples in memory, and no audio bytes or path are returned. No project required.

No captured audio or temporary path is returned or retained. An unavailable/permission-denied backend returns an actionable error or supported:false; no packet or an all-silent route returns a retry instruction and never shows green readiness.

verbs.name: screen_record.recovery_status

It returns only filesystem-safe capture ids, checkpoint/open state, and receipt facts (recovered segment count, exact-or-unknown lost-tail bounds, optional audio first-packet offset, and a source basename). It never exposes cache paths, accepts no arbitrary manifest path, and never probes media, remuxes, repairs, renames, signals, or kills a process. Requires an open project. Use this after project.open or screen_record.start recovery_scan to inspect the durable state after navigation.

verbs.name: screen_record.start
verbs.description: Start one LIVE screen capture in the background (in-process recorder). OPEN-ENDED: when `duration_ms` is OMITTED the capture runs UNTIL screen_record.stop is called (no fixed window — 'record until I stop'); when `duration_ms` IS given it is an optional UPPER BOUND (whichever fires first — the deadline or stop — ends the capture). A second active capture returns conflict until the first capture and its audio worker finish. Required screen_record.doctor cards are checked before any worker starts; unavailable platform dependencies return not_found instead of an asynchronous failed recording. On Windows, the action preflights its exact compact WGC checkpoint output before any capture marker or worker: when it would exceed 260 UTF-16 code units including its terminator, it returns invalid_args synchronously with an instruction to use a shorter project path. On Linux, the action-specific preflight allows only the exact prompt-deferred XDG ScreenCast `screen_capture:unknown` card to reach the user-selected source picker; it never changes Doctor `ready`, and every missing, degraded, or other unknown required card still returns not_found. Before it reserves a new capture it scans prior project-local checkpoint manifests: only a dead owner with a contiguous independently playable finalized prefix is recovered, while live/ambiguous owners are deferred and corrupt journals fail closed. The capture runs on a background thread that, when it ends, writes project.json (a RecordingProject {settings, source_video, audio?, events}) + the source mp4 (+ a mic wav when `audio`, + system.wav when `system_audio`) under <project>/cache/screen_record/<capture_id>/. On Windows, system.wav starts at the first real WASAPI packet and a sibling system-audio.json sidecar {schema:'shellx-cut/system-audio-timing/1', first_packet_offset_ms} records its offset from capture start (null means no packet); older/no-sidecar captures retain zero-offset placement. An external stop flag is registered under capture_id so screen_record.stop can end the recording promptly. A local <dir>/.capture.json recovery marker {pid, duration_ms, open_ended, fps, audio, keys} is atomically published so screen_record.stop still recovers a completed capture even across a cutd restart (the in-memory stop flag is lost on restart, but a capture that finalized on its own bound is still read from the file). Marker metadata never selects an output path: stop always derives the exact local <capture_id>/project.json. cutd's OWN environment (WAYLAND_DISPLAY / XDG_RUNTIME_DIR / DBUS) reaches the recorder's ScreenCast portal. `monitor` is passed through (primary when omitted). Capture state is filesystem-based (no AppState change). Requires an open project.

duration_ms.description: OPTIONAL upper-bound capture length in ms. OMIT for OPEN-ENDED capture ('record until I stop' — ended only by screen_record.stop). When given, the capture ends at this deadline OR at stop, whichever comes first.

audio.description: Also record the microphone (voice narration) → a mic wav muxed at render time (default false).

keys.description: Record keystrokes for the key-cast overlay. OFF by default (privacy: keys can reveal passwords/secrets). Opt-in.

monitor.description: 1-based monitor index to capture (Windows; from screen_record.doctor.monitors). None / 0 = primary. Ignored when `window` is set.

window.description: Capture a single application WINDOW by title (Windows-only; pick from screen_record.doctor.windows). Takes precedence over `monitor`. None = whole monitor/screen.

system_audio.description: Also capture DESKTOP/SYSTEM audio (game/app sound) as a separate track. Linux uses the native PipeWire default-sink monitor and measures its first nonempty packet on the capture clock; a finalized no-packet WAV is null-timed and skipped, while a PipeWire failure removes its partial WAV. Windows uses endpoint-independent process loopback; macOS uses a Core Audio process tap alongside ScreenCaptureKit.

studio.description: Optional initial Recording Studio metadata such as the chosen background. Live camera capture is not available in this release; camera overlay metadata is reserved for downstream composition with an existing camera file.

verbs.result: {capture_id, out_dir, status:"recording", duration_ms, open_ended, studio_events, recovery_scan:{recovered:[capture_id], deferred:[detail], failed_closed:[detail]}, note} — capture_id names a dir under <project>/cache/screen_record/; duration_ms is null + open_ended true for an open-ended capture; studio_events points at the capture's timed composition metadata; recovery_scan reports only this pre-start pass, so query screen_record.recovery_status for durable per-capture receipts; the note flags the one-time XDG ScreenCast consent dialog on the first capture. no_project if no project is open; invalid_args if a Windows project path exceeds the WGC checkpoint limit; not_found if required recorder dependencies are unavailable; conflict if another capture still owns the recording devices.

verbs.name: screen_record.stop
verbs.description: Finalize a capture started by screen_record.start and surface its artifacts. This STOPS the capture — it sets the capture's external stop flag (ending an OPEN-ENDED recording promptly), then waits for the recorder to write its project.json and reads it. For a closed native checkpoint with fewer delivered frames than its measured capture span, finalization materializes the missing span as cloned video frames; contradictory timing remains a fail-closed error. Pipeline: (1) resolve <project>/cache/screen_record/<capture_id>/ (missing → not_found); (1b) SIGNAL stop so an open-ended capture ends now (no-op if cutd restarted and lost the in-memory flag — the file poll still recovers a capture that finalized on its own bound); (2) read local marker duration plus the durable journal start only to derive the exact local <capture_id>/project.json and a finite finalization budget; legacy marker project_path values are ignored; (3) POLL for project.json to exist AND be non-empty for twice the declared/observed capture work plus 15s (45s minimum, 15min maximum; 300ms between checks); never appears → a clean timeout; (4) parse the RecordingProject → extract source_video, audio?, and the embedded events EventTrack, writing the events object to <dir>/events.json (pretty) so it feeds the existing screen_record.autoedit {track} verb; (5) if autoedit:true, chain screen_record.autoedit with the finalized capture settings.fps as config.out_fps so the plan preserves recorded elapsed time, and include the produced plan path. Requires an open project.

capture_id.description: The capture id returned by screen_record.start (names a dir under <project>/cache/screen_record/).

autoedit.description: After finalizing, chain screen_record.autoedit on the events track to produce an EditPlan with the finalized capture FPS as out_fps (default false).

mux_raw.description: RAW CAPTURE mode (default false): after finalizing, fold the capture's video + captured sound sources (mic + system) into ONE standalone raw.mp4 with NO autoedit/zoom/cursor/polish pass, and return it as `raw_path`. Both mic and system present → amix into a single full-level audio track. Pair with autoedit:false to skip ALL post-processing (the Record panel's 'Raw capture' mode).

raw_path.description: Explicit raw recording .mp4 output path (FENCED). Default: the session output dir (project.set_output_dir) or <project>/exports/raw_recording.mp4.

verbs.result: {capture_id, project, source, audio, webcam, events, studio_events, raw_streams, plan, clicks, cursor_samples, cursor_correlation} — project = the finalized project.json path; source = the captured source_video; audio = the mic wav path or null; webcam = the optional captured webcam stream path; events = the written events.json path (feeds screen_record.autoedit); studio_events = the timed composition metadata path when present; raw_streams lists discovered screen/camera/mic/system/studio artifacts plus system_timing when the Windows WASAPI packet-offset sidecar exists; plan = the EditPlan path when autoedit:true (else null); clicks/cursor_samples = the lengths of the events arrays. cursor_correlation = {source, state: exact|approximate|unavailable, exact_clicks, approximate_clicks, unavailable_clicks, max_metadata_age_ms?, detail?}; its click counters are button transitions (press and release). Wayland evdev coordinates are approximate unless paired with fresh PipeWire cursor metadata; X11 and Windows/macOS monitor rdevin desktop coordinates are exact only after a validated capture-surface transform. Linux uses actual finalized video dimensions, and marks rdevin input unavailable if they cannot be established. Windows/macOS window capture has no timestamped rectangle stream, so its rdevin positions are unavailable rather than falsely exact after move or resize. No button transitions report unavailable rather than vacuous exactness. no_project if no project is open; not_found if the capture dir is absent; sidecar if the capture never finalized. RAW MODE adds raw_path (the standalone raw.mp4, null unless mux_raw:true) plus raw_has_mic/raw_has_system.

Requires an open project and a capture_id returned by screen_record.start.

label.description: Optional marker label for recording marker events.

verbs.name: screen_record.autoedit

Uses the linked record-engine in process, writing the plan to <project>/cache/screen_record/<sourcestem>.plan.json. `config` is an optional partial EngineConfig override (max_zoom, zoom timings, cursor/keycast tuning, out_fps, idle tuning); unknown keys are rejected. studio_events.description: Optional project-local path to studio-events.json. Camera events are converted into EditPlan.webcam.timeline for polish replay.

verbs.name: screen_record.polish
verbs.description: The recorder polish pipeline: bake the project-local recorder MP4 (source recording + EditPlan → zoom/speed/cursor polish) and DROP IT ONTO THE TIMELINE. ORCHESTRATOR (like assemble.broll / import.otio): records NO op of its own — wraps the work in an auto-checkpoint and dispatches media.import + edit.add_track + edit.insert as real, replay-safe ops. Pipeline: (1) CONTENT-ADDRESSED bake (the matte pattern) — cache key = source content hash + plan-bytes hash, baked mp4 at <project>/cache/screen_record/<key>.mp4; a hit returns cached:true and skips the bake, a miss renders through the integrated Cut recorder; (2) media.import the baked mp4 and wait for its import chain; (3) ensure the target track exists (default "v1"; an explicit absent `track` is created as a video track) then edit.insert at `at_ms` (default 0, no ripple). A sibling system.wav is imported on its own a_system track; when system-audio.json is present, it starts at first_packet_offset_ms after `at_ms` and is trimmed to the remaining video duration. Missing sidecars retain legacy zero-offset placement. Requires an open project.

source.description: Project-local path to the source recording MP4, normally returned by screen_record.stop.

plan.description: Project-local path to the EditPlan JSON (from screen_record.autoedit).

track.description: Target video track id (default "v1"; created if absent).

at_ms.description: Timeline position to insert the baked clip (default 0).

raw.description: When true, SKIP the slow zoom/cursor/frame re-render: stream-COPY the captured video and mux the mic (near-instant) so 'stop → editable clip' is fast. The EditPlan is still required (cache-keying) but is NOT applied; run polish again without raw for the auto-zoom/cursor pass. Default false (full polish).

Orchestrator: no op of its own; the sub-verbs (media.import, edit.add_track, edit.insert) record the ops, all revertible via the auto-checkpoint.

verbs.name: screen_record.export

Sparse or variable-rate source frames are resampled to the EditPlan FPS before compositing, so a high nominal stream rate cannot duplicate frames and lengthen the planned export. For a direct recorder capture source, MP4 export validates its sibling mic.wav and system.wav artifacts, honors system-audio.json first_packet_offset_ms (or omits a null-timed no-packet system stream), and mixes them through the planned renderer; it never falls back to an unfenced raw-path mux. format "gif": render to a temp mp4 then convert to the fenced .gif (gif_fps default 15, gif_width default 720; the temp mp4 is removed). The immediate response captures the output lease and returns a job_id; poll jobs.status for the finished file, progress, cancellation, or actionable error. The output path is fenced and an explicit `path` must match format, else the session output dir (project.set_output_dir), else <project>/exports/recording.<ext>. Requires an open project (for the fence root).

plan.description: Project-local path to the EditPlan JSON (from screen_record.autoedit).

path.description: Explicit output path matching format (.mp4 or .gif; fenced). Default: the session output dir or <project>/exports/recording.<ext>.

format.description: mp4 (default) = the polished video; gif = render then convert to an animated GIF.

gif_width.description: GIF width px (default 720, height auto; format:"gif" only).

verbs.result: {job_id, path, format, status:"queued"} — the fenced destination is reserved before this response returns. Poll jobs.status(job_id): done.result = {path, format, frames, elapsed_ms}; failed.error is actionable. invalid_args on an unknown format.

verbs.name: system.fetch_tool
verbs.description: Consented download + install of a MISSING runtime tool, as a background job (returns {job_id}; progress via the jobs domain + job_progress events). SECURITY (hard, path-fencing model): the tool id comes from a BUILT-IN registry ONLY (v1: "ffmpeg") — there is NO caller-supplied URL surface, so this is not a fetch-arbitrary-URL primitive. The URL is an https-pinned BtbN FFmpeg-Builds release asset selected BY OS (linux64-gpl.tar.xz / win64-gpl.zip); the archive's sha256 is verified against the release's checksums.sha256 BEFORE anything is installed; the payload is staged in a temp dir and ATOMICALLY moved into the app-data tools dir (the exact dir the cut-media toolpath resolver checks, rung 3) only after verification. On success the doctor re-scans and a doctor_updated event fires — the ffmpeg card flips missing→bundled-or-appdata. rationale is recorded on the job. OS-aware: the Linux asset is fetched+installed live here; the Windows asset path is selected by OS and documented for the cold-notebook session.

tool.description: Built-in registry id of the tool to download. v1: "ffmpeg" (installs both ffmpeg + ffprobe from one BtbN archive). Unknown ids fail fast — there is deliberately no URL arg.

verbs.result: {job_id, tool} — watch job_progress (download% → verifying → installing) or poll jobs.status; the job result is {tool, installed_dir, version, sha256, source_url, bytes, ffmpeg_ok_after}; doctor_updated fires on completion

verbs.name: system.setup_perception
verbs.description: Consented provisioning of the Python PERCEPTION venv (transcription + silence/scenes/beats + auto-reframe), as a background job (returns {job_id}; progress via the jobs domain + job_progress events). The installer ships only the sidecar SCRIPT (instruments.py + pinned requirements.txt); this builds the heavy venv on first run, with consent. SECURITY (path-fencing model, same model as system.fetch_tool): it downloads `uv` (Astral's static Python provisioner) ONLY through the built-in fetch allow-list (https-pinned astral-sh/uv release, per-asset sha256 verified before use) — NO caller-supplied URL. It then has uv install a standalone CPython 3.12 (system python is too old on real desktops — macOS ships 3.9, below the onnx-asr ≥3.10 floor), create the app-data sidecar venv, and `uv pip install -r` the BUNDLED requirements (onnx-asr Parakeet/Canary STT, torchaudio MMS_FA alignment, and the perception stack). On success the doctor re-scans and the `perception` card flips missing→ready. rationale is recorded on the job.

warm_model.description: Pre-download the default Parakeet ONNX model during setup so the FIRST transcription is instant (default true). Set false to skip — selected models then lazy-download on first transcribe.

verbs.result: {job_id} — watch job_progress (downloading uv → installing Python → creating venv → installing dependencies → downloading model) or poll jobs.status; the job result is {venv_python, uv_version, onnx_asr_ready, model_warmed, perception_ok_after}; doctor_updated fires on completion

verbs.name: system.setup_matte
verbs.description: Make AI BACKGROUND REMOVAL (edit.matte) usable LOCALLY — the seamless, one-click install of the user-side matte runtime (the ffmpeg pattern; the user NEVER runs pip or sees a terminal). With NO args: DOWNLOAD the 14 MB RVM model (PeterL1n/RobustVideoMatting v1.0.0, sha256-pinned) into the app-data matte dir, as a background job (returns {job_id}; progress via the jobs domain). onnxruntime rides the PERCEPTION venv (so for anyone who's set up perception the install is just the model). With `path`: BROWSE-to-existing — point at an rvm.onnx already on disk (validated + persisted, synchronous). On success the doctor `matte` card flips missing -> ready. The runtime is invisible plumbing cutd manages (a one-shot CLI spawned per bake, like the perception sidecar) — one app, no second window. OPTIONAL — core editing + render work without it. RVM is GPL: we ship integration, the user installs the model on consent.

model.description: Which background-removal tier to install. Default rvm (portable, AUTOMATIC, license-clean, CPU-ok). matanyone = the PREMIUM opt-in (MatAnyone2 — NVIDIA, non-commercial, target-assigned, cleaner edges).

path.description: Browse-to-existing: a model file already on disk (rvm.onnx, or matanyone2.pth when model=matanyone). Omit to download.

accept_noncommercial.description: REQUIRED to install model=matanyone: explicit acceptance that the MatAnyone2 weights are NON-COMMERCIAL (NTU S-Lab License 1.0). Download happens on your consent and responsibility. Without it the verb returns an invalid_args licence notice.

Flips the matte / matte_premium doctor card.

verbs.description: Read one live or retained ShellX Motion render job for the active Cut project. Cut derives the stable caller identity internally and never accepts Motion's operator-only cross-caller scope. The result preserves Motion's pending|running|succeeded|failed|cancelled|skipped state vocabulary and omits caller hashes, process ids, runtime roots, and receipt paths.

verbs.name: motion.script_to_cut

Used by Generate scripted-video templates and exposed directly for agent/debug workflows. Preview policy is non-mutating and returns PNG/receipt/artifact evidence. Insert policy requires an open project, real render output, and lowers to normal project.checkpoint/media.import/edit.insert ops so replay and undo stay owned by Cut.

script_path.description: Path to a shellx-motion/scripted-video@1 JSON file.

out_dir.description: Optional output directory for scripted JSON, Motion package/render/receipt artifacts. Defaults under the open project, or temp for preview with no project.

duration_ms.description: Optional timeline/source duration override. Defaults to the rendered Motion package duration.

verbs.name: motion.map_import
verbs.description: Validate and map a ShellX Motion shellx-motion/cut-import-plan@1 JSON file into the Cut verbs it would lower to. rendered_media plans require attested media handles. Current SDK handoffs carrying shellx-motion/package-render-lineage@1 must bind the same two-hash package lineage (or five-hash adapter.gltf lineage) through the reference, descriptor identity, exact render receipt and Cut-plan receipt; results report status:'verified'. When packageDir is supplied, Cut independently derives bounded current package lineage and reports currentPackage.status as exact, changed, or unavailable without changing immutable artifact authorization. Legacy template/script connector handles remain compatible only with render+connector receipt binding and report status:'legacy-unverified' without claiming package lineage. The rendered operation/source/media/reference shapes are closed and mismatches fail before paths are exposed. editable_lowering plans are receipt-bound and accepted only when every field maps exactly to an enabled native Cut operation; unsupported/dynamic fields fail with a rendered-media recovery action. The native receiver materializes the document background as a full-canvas shape, maps text plus rect/ellipse/line shapes to title.add/edit.add_shape, lowers uniform opacity and transform.x/transform.y tracks to clip-local opacity/pos_x/pos_y edit.keyframe points (including off-screen positions), lowers exact non-overlapping fade-in/out transitions, and accepts existing Cut video or unprocessed audio assets through bounded cut-asset:<id> references. Mixed easing and transform scale/rotation automation fail closed. Always non-mutating.

path.description: Path to a shellx-motion/cut-import-plan@1 JSON file.

packageDir.description: Optional Motion package directory used to resolve dry-run plannedPath values and independently derive path-free currentPackage exact|changed|unavailable lineage evidence. Real artifacts are resolved only through their verified root-relative handle.

verbs.result: {ok:true, schema:'shellx-cut/motion-import-map@1', planPath, packageDir?, packageId, motionId, targetId, mode, integration, operationCount, operations, renderedMedia, artifactHandles, lineageProofs, planned, warnings}. lineageProofs are path-free shellx-cut/motion-import-attestation@1 records with verified|legacy-unverified artifact status; handle/operation/descriptor identity; immutable package lineage; currentPackage:{schema,status:exact|changed|unavailable,lineage?,changedFields,reason?}; and receipt identities. Always non-mutating. editable_lowering planned rows name their normal Cut verbs and sourceLayerId; artifactHandles and lineageProofs are empty.

verbs.name: motion.apply_import
verbs.description: Dry-run or apply a ShellX Motion shellx-motion/cut-import-plan@1 JSON file into the open Cut project. rendered_media plans enforce the same verified versus legacy-unverified attestation policy as motion.map_import, independently report optional current package lineage as exact, changed, or unavailable, atomically stage media/inserts, and persist the immutable path-free originAttestation on each replay-backed motion_link across undo/redo, reopen, refresh and relink. editable_lowering plans validate the complete plan first, create normal native Cut title/shape objects, lower supported opacity and x/y position automation, bind each sourceLayerId to its stable clip identity, and group the native operations plus mapping record into one undo/redo action. A changed plan for the same package/motion identity updates those objects and creates, replaces, or clears supported keyframe tracks in place when source-layer identities, native kinds, and timing still match. Failures auto-revert to the pre-plan checkpoint; unknown or unsupported dynamic payloads fail closed to rendered media. The exact plan SHA-256 remains the idempotency key. background:true queues real apply through jobs.*.

path.description: Path to a shellx-motion/cut-import-plan@1 JSON file.

packageDir.description: Optional Motion package directory used to resolve dry-run plannedPath values and independently derive path-free currentPackage exact|changed|unavailable lineage evidence. Real artifacts are resolved only through their verified root-relative handle.

dryRun.description: true = non-mutating validation/preflight; false = apply attested rendered media or exact supported native editable operations.

background.description: With dryRun:false, queue the attestation/apply as a cancellable background job and return its job_id immediately.

verbs.result: Synchronous/dry-run: {ok:true, schema:'shellx-cut/motion-import-apply@1', dryRun, wouldMutate, planPath, packageDir?, packageId, motionId, targetId, mode, integration, lineageProofs, idempotencyKey?, alreadyApplied?, reimported?, checkpoint?, planned, bindings?, mappingOpId?, import?, insert?, imports?, inserts?, op_ids?, clips?, assets?, rollback?, warnings, restore_hint?}. Each rendered lineageProof includes currentPackage:{schema,status:exact|changed|unavailable,lineage?,changedFields,reason?}; a real rendered apply persists the complete proof as motion_link.originAttestation. background:true returns a cancellable jobs.* handle.

verbs.name: motion.link.refresh
verbs.description: Rerender a linked Motion media clip from the latest verified Canvas copy-on-write handback when one exists, otherwise from its bound local package, into a NEW immutable project-owned artifact. Cut revalidates package identity and the exact authored-source revision, verifies the Motion receipt and output digest, then atomically replaces the clip source in place. The Cut clip id, timeline slot, trim/look/effects, and previous rendered fallback are preserved. Any handback, render, receipt, source-race, project-race, or commit failure leaves the last good clip untouched. One replay-safe and undoable motion.link.refresh op owns the new asset plus edit.replace lowering.

clip.description: Stable Cut clip id carrying shellx-cut/motion-link@1 provenance.

preset.description: Motion video export preset. H.264 is the interoperable default.

job_id.description: Optional caller-chosen Motion job id for live observation through motion.job.get while this blocking refresh render runs.

verbs.result: {ok:true, schema:'shellx-cut/motion-link-refresh@1', clip, asset, job_id, motion_job_id?, packageId, motionId, sourceRevision, render:{path,sha256,byteLength,preset}, lastReceiptId?, receiptPath, canvasReturn?:{applied,sessionToken,revisionToken,completedAtUnixMs,sourceRevision}, state:'linked-current', restore_hint}. job_id is Cut's post-render media-enrichment job; motion_job_id is the separate Motion render handle. receiptPath is read from Motion's supported render envelope and retained as lastReceiptPath in the replay-backed link; canvasReturn is path-free evidence that the latest verified Canvas revision became the link source; project.undo restores the previous source.

verbs.name: motion.link.relink
verbs.description: Repair a linked Motion clip's machine-local package path without changing pixels. Cut canonicalizes the directory, validates manifest.json + motion.json, and refuses a package whose packageId/motionId differs from the durable link identity. The link becomes source-dirty until an explicit refresh succeeds.

clip.description: Stable Cut clip id carrying shellx-cut/motion-link@1 provenance.

package_dir.description: Existing local ShellX Motion package directory containing manifest.json and motion.json.

verbs.result: {ok:true, schema:'shellx-cut/motion-link-relink@1', clip, packageDir, packageId, motionId, sourceRevision, state:'source-dirty'}. Non-pixel metadata op; use motion.link.refresh to render and attach it.

verbs.name: motion.link.edit
verbs.description: Open a rendered linked clip's verified local package in ShellX Canvas Motion Studio. Cut canonicalizes the source and re-checks packageId/motionId, creates an immutable project-local return request, then launches the configured Canvas executable with a fixed argv array: --motion-package <canonical-dir> --motion-cut-return-request <canonical-request>. Canvas keeps both paths in its trusted host, validates the package with the local Motion SDK, opens a path-free editable revision, and publishes immutable ready descriptors only after verified renders. No Cut timeline mutation and no shell command interpolation.

clip.description: Stable Cut clip id carrying shellx-cut/motion-link@1 provenance.

verbs.result: {ok:true, schema:'shellx-cut/motion-link-edit@1', clip, packageId, motionId, launched:true, pid?, returnChannel:{state:'pending',pathPrivate:true}, localOnly:true, remotePublish:false}. Set SHELLX_CANVAS_BIN when shellx-canvas is not on PATH.

verbs.name: motion.link.tracking.inventory
verbs.description: Inspect the path-free tracking/stabilization inventory for a linked local Motion package. Returns document bounds, available package-local video asset ids, visual target layer ids, and persisted lifecycle summaries without exposing host paths. Read-only and local-only.

verbs.name: motion.link.tracking.request
verbs.description: Run deterministic local point or planar tracking against a manifest-declared package video asset. Cut accepts a normalized seed region, compiles it to source pixels, invokes Motion with a fixed argv array, verifies package/receipt/lifecycle identity, and attaches the copy-on-write analysis package only if the linked source did not race. Analysis does not change rendered pixels.

verbs.name: motion.link.tracking.inspect
verbs.description: Inspect one persisted Motion tracking lifecycle and verify that its package-local source bytes still match the recorded identity. Read-only; strips package paths and raw artifact paths from the Cut response.
verbs.result: {ok:true, schema:'shellx-cut/motion-tracking-inspect@1', clip, analysisId, lifecycle, source:{assetId,current,sha256,byteLength}, current, receipt, warnings, localOnly:true}.

verbs.name: motion.link.tracking.apply
verbs.description: Compile a current persisted Motion track into ordinary transform keyframes on a selected visual layer. Motion writes a copy-on-write package and receipt; Cut validates output identity and atomically updates only the linked source binding. The existing Cut render remains the fallback until motion.link.refresh succeeds.

verbs.description: Verify that a Motion layer's tracking attachment, generated keyframes, lifecycle, and package-local source identity remain current. Read-only and path-free.
verbs.result: {ok:true, schema:'shellx-cut/motion-tracking-verify@1', clip, layerId, analysisId?, verification:{attached,current,reasons,...}, lifecycle, source, receipt, warnings, localOnly:true}.

verbs.description: Detach Motion stabilization from a selected layer and restore the exact prior transform keyframes recorded by Motion. The copy-on-write package and receipt are validated before Cut updates the linked source; refresh remains explicit and the prior rendered fallback stays usable.
